about: Lessons for building map pieces for Living City, learnt from the owner's compiles, walks and words (November 2026) and from reading their City 18 map. One entry per lesson: what to do, why (the owner's own words where there are some), how the tools do it, and what checks it. Read with: python3 _dev/tools/map_lessons.py (--tag TAG, --find WORD, --md to rewrite docs/dev/city18-reference.md).

lessons.title: A thing is a prop, never brushes
lessons.rule: Doors, bars, gates, beds, tables, shelves, lamps, speakers, fences, railings, pipes, signs, machines, vehicles, guns, tools: find the Half-Life 2 model and place it. Brushes are for architecture (walls, floors, slabs, steps, frames, kerbs, roofs) and for things no game has a model of (say which in the module's 'Left as brushes' line).
lessons.why: "You use almost entirely brushes to make things when there are perfectly good props ... it literally looks like something from 1998 ... cell doors out of brushes, but there is a whole selection of cell doors and prison bars from HL2 Nova Prospekt ... a loudspeaker out of brushes but there is literally a loudspeaker prop" (20 November).
lessons.how: grep -i WORD _dev/tools/dl/ValveQCs.txt | grep -iE 'source/(hl2|episodic|lostcoast)/'; sizes with map_assets.size(model). docs/dev/map-modules.md, 'Things'.

lessons.title: The prop must be the right thing, not just a thing
lessons.rule: Use the model made for the job: valve wheels (props_pipes valvewheel001/002) not a cart wheel, steel pipes for pressure mains not concrete culvert sections, the Combine's own crates (models/items/item_item_crate) and ration packages (models/weapons/w_package) in a Combine depot, weapon world models (models/weapons/w_*) on a gun rack.
lessons.why: Review, 20 November: a cart wheel on a flood valve, drain culverts as service mains, brush guns on a rack.
lessons.how: Search the lists by what the thing is, not by what is near in size.

lessons.title: A physics prop is never a prop_static
lessons.rule: A model with prop_data (tables, chairs, shelves, lockers, boards, pots, crates, mattresses...) is deleted by the compiler as a prop_static. Place it as prop_dynamic_override (standing still) or prop_physics (loose).
lessons.why: The owner's compile of the town, 20 November: "almost none of the props are showing"; vbsp printed "prop_static using model X, which must be used on a dynamic entity (i.e. prop_physics). Deleted." for every one.
lessons.how: m.static does it by itself (map_assets.is_static / is_physics_prop).
lessons.check: map_assets.py fails a physics model used as prop_static or plain prop_dynamic

lessons.title: Keep networked props to what a place needs
lessons.rule: Every prop_dynamic(_override), prop_physics and prop_door_rotating is an entity the server networks (the game has about 8,000 for everything). About 60 a module at most; clutter that does not need to move should be a model built static.
lessons.why: Follows from physics-props-dynamic: the town went to about 300 such entities.
lessons.how: grep -c the classnames in the built VMF. Valve's maps hold a median of about 105 prop_physics each (22 to 199; 2 in d3_citadel_01), and 421 prop_dynamic in 22 maps (45% parented to moving things such as trains and lifts, 35% named for the game, 20% unnamed train seats, racks and locks) and only 15 with a DefaultAnim (bunker guns); wheels, windmills and rings turn as func_rotating.

lessons.title: A door that opens is the city's own, fitted as the owner's
lessons.rule: Doors players use are prop_door_rotating with door01_left, set up as the owner's 134 are, in an opening 50 wide (from 2 behind the hinge) and 110 high, the door's middle 55 up. The jambs fill the reveal so nothing is seen past the door.
lessons.why: "The apartments' door frames are slightly too large for the doors and I can see past the door into the apartments" (20 November). Measured round 42 of the owner's doors. Valve fits door01_left (49 wide, 109 tall) in a doorway 48 wide and 108 high, two side by side in 96 by 108 (d1_trainstation_02 to 05).
lessons.how: map_town.real_door and door_hole.

lessons.title: A doorway nobody can use never shows a real door
lessons.rule: Never put the door01_left model (or any door that looks openable) where it does not open: board the doorway up (planks, wood_board props), chain it, or brick it.
lessons.why: "The door prop you used for all these unopenable doors is the same prop ... for actual doors that are supposed to open, so it's confusing and I can't tell where I can actually go in" (20 November).
lessons.how: map_town.facade boards unused doorways; heavy doors that never open (lock, swing bridge) still to fix.
lessons.check: map_lint.py door (a door model that is not a prop_door_rotating)

lessons.title: Steps about 16 high and 24 deep
lessons.rule: Fewer, larger steps: rise about 16, tread about 24 (the same slope as 8 and 12, half the steps). (Valve's train station steps rise 8 under a player clip ramp, as the owner's own map does.)
lessons.why: "It's like a stairway meant for toddlers or old ladies? these steps should be fewer and larger" (20 November). Measured in City 18 (20 November): the owner's own flights are mostly 8 up and 12 deep (about 300 steps of 8, 36 of 16), so 16 by 24 is their choice for the long flights of the new pieces (the canal's way up), not a copy of their map. Valve's other maps (21 November): 8 by 12 in all six with stairs (100 to 251 steps a map); 16 by 24 only at d1_trainstation_02's outdoor steps (42).
lessons.how: m.steps does it; hand-made stairs should match. Valve's canals: every one of 205 brush steps measured rises 8 and runs 12; ladders are metalladder002 pieces of 128, most one or two pieces high.

lessons.title: A stair along a wall has a solid open side
lessons.rule: Give a wall stair an upstand (a parapet about 32 high following the flight) on its open side and fill under it to the floor, so it reads as one built stair, not a row of blocks hung on the wall.
lessons.why: Review, 20 November: from the canal the quay, arcade, lift and pipes stairs read as a sawtooth.
lessons.how: m.stair_side(start, run, v1, v2, z_low, z_high, sign): an upstand on the open side of a flight along u.

lessons.title: Pieces meet: no gaps between walls, banks and steps
lessons.rule: Where something stands at a cut in the canal's banks, it fills to the cut's edge: the banks are cut a whole 64 square at a time by m.no_bank. Side walls of steps go down to the floor.
lessons.why: "The geometry in the canal entrance thing has a gap for the sloped walls and the grey concrete brush underneath the railings, there is a gap on both sides" (20 November).
lessons.how: map_town.landing: cheeks 64 wide, solid to the floor.

lessons.title: Nothing floats, nothing is sunk, nothing clips
lessons.rule: Every prop touches a floor, a ceiling, a wall or another prop; lamps sit on their ceilings; bodies lie on the ground they are on (work out a mound's height from the build's bumps).
lessons.why: Floating dome lamps and props in walls found in several modules (20 November); the owner saw floating ropes in the garden.
lessons.how: m.static takes the floor z the thing stands ON; map_assets sizes.
lessons.check: map_floating.py (props touching nothing), the build's LOOK lines (props in walls, through roofs, under floors)

lessons.title: No ropes hanging in the air
lessons.rule: A rope or cable is tied at both ends to something that is there (a pole, a wall, a hook), or it is not placed.
lessons.why: "Please remove the floating ropes in the garden" (20 November).
lessons.how: m.rope: check both ends.
lessons.check: map_lint.py rope (a rope end tied to nothing)

lessons.title: No open pipe end shows its inside
lessons.rule: Cap every pipe end players can see (props_pipes pipe02_connector01, pipe_cap005, a cone or plate brush), and never leave a nodraw face where it can be seen.
lessons.why: "At the end of the pipe for the distillery we need a cone brush or something since the pipe has nodraw on the exposed end" (20 November).
lessons.how: The still: a cap and a funnel (map_mods_b.frustum).

lessons.title: Water never shares a plane with a floor
lessons.rule: A water brush's top sits at least 2 under any floor it lies beneath, or the two flicker through each other.
lessons.why: Review, 20 November: the flood room's drained water lies exactly at its floor.
lessons.how: Fix in map_mods_c.py (the func_water_analog's box to FL - 2).
lessons.check: map_lint.py water (a water brush's top level with a floor)

lessons.title: A fire in a drum stays in the drum
lessons.rule: env_fire falls to the ground under it unless spawnflag 16 (Don't drop) is set: set it for any fire placed above the ground (drums, braziers, stoves).
lessons.why: "The burn barrels flanking the podium have fire on the ground inside the barrel instead of the fire coming out the top" (20 November).
lessons.how: map_mods_b.fire(..., drop=False).
lessons.check: map_lint.py fire (an env_fire on a prop without spawnflag 16)

lessons.title: The loose mattress lies on its back unless turned
lessons.rule: Turn furnituremattress001a over (roll 180) when placing it.
lessons.why: "The mattresses in the clinic are all rotated 180 degrees on their side" (20 November).
lessons.how: map_mods_b.mattress(). Valve places furnituremattress001a as a prop_ragdoll (17 of 18 in 22 maps), angles 0 yaw 0, spawnflags 4, on the floor of bunk rooms and hideouts (c01a, c03, c05, c06, c10, c12, ts03, ts04), never as a static.

lessons.title: What Half-Life 2 made move, moves
lessons.rule: Swings, roundabouts, hanging things: physics props on phys_hinge (or ropes parented to them), not frozen models.
lessons.why: "HL2 had a working merry-go-round, and working swings" (20 November).
lessons.how: map_mods_b.swing; the playground's roundabout.

lessons.title: A gate goes in its frame
lessons.rule: Nova Prospekt's interior_fence002e is the frame for the gate interior_fence001g: hang the gate in the frame (or use the gate alone), never the frame as the gate.
lessons.why: "The gates you used are the gate/door frames for the real gate interior_fence001g; so they have to be fitted inside of the gate frames, or just used instead" (20 November).
lessons.how: The pit: frame static, the gate riding an unseen swing door.

lessons.title: A lamppost's arm reaches over what it lights
lessons.rule: lamppost03a's arm runs along the model's +y (90 degrees left of its yaw): turn it so the arm is over the street or the place, never over a wall or a drop behind.
lessons.why: "The lamppost at the top of the canal entry stairs is backwards and should be facing the street not the stairs" (20 November).
lessons.how: Yaw so model +y points at the street.

lessons.title: A lit lamp uses the lit model
lessons.rule: Where a light shines, the fixture is its _on model (light_cagelight02_on, not _off with a light under it); a dead lamp has no light.
lessons.why: Review, 20 November: overflow, thumper, railbridge and armoury.
lessons.how: m.lamp uses real fixtures. Valve's lit lamp models carry an env_sprite at the bulb (114 of 149, distance 0): materials/sprites/light_glow03.vmt, scale .75, rendermode 9 (world space glow), renderamt 255; 147 of 149 have a light entity within reach (all lamps: light_spot 475, point_spotlight 202, light 111). Our m.lamp glows at scale 0.25.
lessons.check: map_lint.py offlamp (an _off fixture with a light at it)

lessons.title: Light as City 18 does: many small fixtures, some with beams
lessons.rule: Light a room with two or three fixtures, not one; point some (light_spot, point_spotlight); use the city's own fixtures: dome lights, lab fluorescent tubes indoors, cage lights in service places, the Combine's light on Combine places, lampposts outside.
lessons.why: The owner's map: 597 lights, 391 light_spot, 174 point_spotlight; dome light 151, lab fluorescent 149, Combine light 75, lamp fixture 52, cage light 47. Lampposts in City 18 stand 360 to 870 apart (most about 600 to 750). Valve's day streets use the unlit lamppost03a_off with no light on it, 818 (d3_c17_13) and 962 (d1_trainstation_04) apart; lampfixture01a 784 apart round the plaza (d1_trainstation_02).
lessons.how: m.lamp, m.spot, m.light; every canal stretch now gets a caged lamp on every third rib, a third of them dead (dress_canal_walls).

lessons.title: Lay grime on: stains, cracks, trash, posters, signs
lessons.rule: Every place gets overlays and decals: water stains down walls and under drains, cracks, trash in corners, posters where people are, the lambda where the Resistance is, danger signs on hazards, numbers on machines.
lessons.why: The owner's map: 249 info_overlays and 267 infodecals (decalstain002a 26 times, trashdecal04a, plaster cracks, Breen posters, danger signs, metal grates, speaker grilles, graffiti 059a, the lambda spray). The modules had almost none.
lessons.how: m.grime(kind, u, v, z) with GRIME's kinds (stain, drain, trash, crack, poster, danger, graffiti, number, lambda, burn, puddle, grate, debris, police: all checked in Valve's lists); every canal stretch now gets drain stains and some graffiti by itself (map_modules.dress_canal_walls). Valve's 13 canal maps: 613 infodecal and 75 info_overlay; the commonest are ivy (ivy01 to ivy03: 187), trash (trashdecal01a and 02a: 121), decalstain002a 17, decalconcretedrain002a 17 (and 11 overlays), lambdaspray_2a 14 (1 to 5 a map: the Resistance's way marks), graffiti001b/c/d 31. GRIME has no ivy: add a kind "ivy" (decals/ivy01, ivy02, ivy03) for canal walls. Decals go with props in Valve's maps: loose trash has a trash decal (trashdecal01a, 02a) within 48 in 57% of cases, bins 42%, benches 45% (decalstain014a, debris_concrete001a), shelves 43%, chairs 40% (decalstain002a, bloodstain_001), corpses 25% (blood, scorch1), barrels and crates only 11%.

lessons.title: Every place sounds like itself
lessons.rule: Each module and each part of the town names a soundscape (env_soundscape with a radius), not only an ambient_generic loop.
lessons.why: The owner's map: 155 env_soundscapes (d1_trainstation.*, d1_town.*, prison.*, d1_canals.*, construct.inside...) and only 41 ambient_generics.
lessons.how: m.soundscape(SCAPES[kind], u, v, z, radius): SCAPES holds the soundscapes the owner's own map uses (tunnel, watery, slime, pump, cave, flat, house, inside, combine, laundry, metal, courtyard, square, rooftop). Valve's station puts two env_soundscape at each change of place (d1_trainstation.Platform, .Turnstyle, .Interrogation, .QuietCourtyard, general.concrete_quiet). Valve's 13 canal maps: 173 env_soundscape (8 to 24 a map), commonest canals_slime_tunnel 17, d1_canals.general_dripping_tunnel 13, canals_river 12, canals_slime_outside 10, canals_canal_water_industrial 10; also canals_canal_water, canals_canal_nowater (a dry canal: fits ours), canals_tunnel_dry and canals_tunnel_wet.

lessons.title: Streets as the owner's: pavements, kerbs, a crowned road
lessons.rule: Pavements 96 wide at the floor's height with a kerb of 8; gutters 8 down; cobbles (stonefloor006d_c17, sett strips 006e/006f) rising to a crown 4 over the gutters.
lessons.why: "The street is just flat cobblestone? We have sidewalks and a sloped street (higher in middle) all over the main map"; "sidewalks are not 2 feet tall irl, they are like 6-12 inches" (20 November). Measured in the owner's map. Valve's own City 17 streets for comparison (measured 21 November): roadway 256 (d1_trainstation_03, 04) or 320 (d3_c17_13), flat (crown 0 in 34 of 36 and 79 of 83 sections), the kerb a plain step of 4 (8 on 62 of 166 kerbs of the war street), pavements 128 to 192 of concretefloor028c, roads concretefloor033c or stonefloor006d_c17 with 006f_c17 edge strips. The owner's crown and kerb of 8 are their own choice: keep them.
lessons.how: map_town.lay_street. The street corridor beside the canal does not have it yet.

lessons.title: Building fronts, not brick walls
lessons.rule: Dress a building line as houses: lots of different heights, a plinth, a string course, a cornice, pilasters between neighbours, windows recessed with sills and lintels, downpipes, real doors where there is a way in.
lessons.why: "There's no design, windows, building facades, nothing! I was hoping you'd make something more similar to the city just on a much smaller scale" (20 November).
lessons.how: map_town.facade.

lessons.title: Not every window the same glass
lessons.rule: Use several of the owner's glass materials, each laid exactly as their map lays it, a different one per house.
lessons.why: "The window texture fits right but it's the same texture and it looks awful because every window looks like that; we need to use the varieties of glass" (20 November).
lessons.how: map_town.GLASS: six fits read from the owner's map.

lessons.title: Cut corners and a broken skyline
lessons.rule: Corner buildings get a cut (chamfered) corner, often with a doorway; rooflines get chimneys, aerials, dishes, the odd pitched roof; facades get balconies, shutters, shopfronts with signs and awnings.
lessons.why: City 18's massing (octagonal columns, cut corners, stepped blocks); review of the town, 20 November.
lessons.how: map_town.facade puts chimneys, aerials, dishes and vents on the roofs (roof_prop, one to a slot so they never stand in each other), a pitched roof on about one house in three, balconies on some upper floors, awnings and name boards over shop windows. The houses are filled 640 deep behind their fronts and the sky over inner roofs starts at the lid, so things can stand on them. Cut corners are still to do.

lessons.title: A town is not one straight line
lessons.rule: Lay a town as an L or a U (corners), keeping the two arms' modules apart behind a corner (a stretch of house fronts alone, 1280 long, on the inner side).
lessons.why: "Yes I think the town needs to be in an L shape or a U" (20 November).
lessons.how: Layout words 'turn right|left' and 'houses N' (map_town.corner).

lessons.title: On a street, places sit at the pavement's height
lessons.rule: A module lifted from the canal to a street drops the terraces it needed against the canal's floods: its yards sit level with the pavement; where something must be higher, steps from the pavement reach it.
lessons.why: "Please lower the playground to be flush/even with the sidewalk and not raised up on a massive platform"; "the playground needs stairs to get up the slope" (20 November).
lessons.how: Modules read m.fr.dz (on a street when non-zero); map_town.terrace_slopes makes steps.

lessons.title: Rooms with room in them
lessons.rule: Leave walking room: furniture against walls, a clear path through every room and into every stall; split a crowded room's things into two rooms; no prop inside another.
lessons.why: "You put a couch inside the table and the wood furnace/stove is almost touching the table and couch and it's just too cramped, half of that can go in the bedroom(s)"; "all the market stalls are filled with boxes and random props and there's no room to even walk into them" (20 November).
lessons.how: Place by the models' real boxes (map_assets.size).
lessons.check: map_lint.py overlap (a solid prop inside another), printed as LOOK lines by every build

lessons.title: Interiors in City 18's way
lessons.rule: Plaster walls in two tones split by a dado rail, wooden floors, door casings proud of the wall, a ceiling trim; stoves, sinks, toilets, fridges, iron bunks backs to the wall; radiators; fluorescent tubes. Never a plain cream box. Each kind of place in its own materials: a cellar is brick or stone, a Combine room is Combine metal, a culvert is damp concrete.
lessons.why: The owner's flats (picture), their 14 toilets and sinks; review, 20 November (cream rooms in a dozen modules). Valve's flats (d1_trainstation_03) for comparison: four inside walls in five are one material floor to ceiling; where two-toned the change is at 64.
lessons.how: Line rooms with thin detail brushes; the plan's own walls are concrete or brick.

lessons.title: The Combine's places in the Combine's kit
lessons.rule: Use the Combine's own props: booths (combine_booth_short01a/med01a), buttresses (combinebuttress), bunker shields, fences with fields (combine_fence01a/b, combine_emitter01), railings (props_combine railing_128/256/512), lights (combine_light001/002), monitors, cameras (combinecamera001), locks, health chargers, metal (metalcombine002).
lessons.why: The owner's map: combine_fence01a/b 12 each, combine_light002a 75; review, 20 November (checkpoint, thumper, depot, armoury in brushes, prison fencing and cream plaster).
lessons.how: grep source/hl2/props_combine in the lists. Into the old city the Combine comes as models (combine_barricade_*, combine_lock01, monitors, CombineInnerwallCluster1024, combine_light002a); its brushes are rare: 34 in d1_trainstation_02, metalcombine001 panels 4 to 8 thick, a third of them cut into the old wall, none in d1_trainstation_03 to 05.

lessons.title: Do not replace what the owner liked
lessons.rule: When going through a module, keep what the owner praised or asked for (the pit's hanging lamps); change only what is wrong.
lessons.why: "Ok wait you went a tad bit too far: the fighting pit/ring had really cool lights above it before and you replaced them with street lights, please reverse that" (20 November).
lessons.how: Read the module's history (git log -p) before reworking it.

lessons.title: The auditorium sinks from the street; its speaker is on the wall
lessons.rule: The plaza's top row is at the street; the rostrum at the back wall faces the street; the loudspeaker is mounted on the wall, not on lampposts.
lessons.why: "Can we rotate the speaker/auditorium module 180 degrees so that the auditorium begins (highest row) at street/sidewalk level and recedes/sinks down"; "replace the light posts above the podium and put the loudspeaker on the wall instead" (20 November).
lessons.how: map_mods_b.m_plaza.

lessons.title: Garden beds carry planting spots
lessons.rule: Mark where the game can plant (melons, pumpkins): about 8 info_targets lc_garden_plot_N on the beds, evenly spread but each a little off line and turned.
lessons.why: "Make the garden beds have some sort of entity or brush that allows the gamemode to register the beds as planting spots, with about 8 evenly but slightly off kilter (not robotic AI perfect) planting spots" (20 November).
lessons.how: map_mods_b.m_garden. The game does not plant yet (TODO.md).

lessons.title: Possible headquarters carry a pole marker
lessons.rule: Put an info_target named lc_hq_setup... where the Resistance's flagpole should stand; the game stands a bare pole at every one, territory or not.
lessons.why: "I didn't see the flag entity or flagpole in the town map"; "yes, always stand a bare pole at the markers" (20 November).
lessons.how: m.target('lc_hq_setup_NAME', ...); sv_livingcity_base.lua B.Poles.

lessons.title: Episode Two models when the owner asks; check them first
lessons.rule: Episode Two's models are allowed where the owner asks for them (the tram's passenger cars), noted by map_assets. Check each: the EP2 intro cars (passengercar_intro01a/b/c) have no collision and draw about 4800 units from their origin, so passengercar001 and _dam01 are used instead.
lessons.why: "Can we just use the train props from EP2 that you start EP2 inside? they are perfectly sized and already built" (20 November).
lessons.how: map_assets.size and the model's QC.

lessons.title: The owner's sewers carry water; the open canal is dry
lessons.rule: Under the city the owner's sewers (floor about z 268, water nature/sewer_waterdarkfog2 to z 291) run water in a channel with raised walks either side and round-arched tunnel mouths: a piece that joins the sewers (the drain module's far end) should match that. The open canal, built by these tools and compiled by the owner (the ring and the first canal), is dry with mud: canal modules match it as they are.
lessons.why: Measured in c18_lc.vmf, 20 November: the water in reference pictures 06 and 15 is the sewer's (4 water brushes in the whole map: the sewers' two, a pool, and the sea), not a canal's. An earlier note here said the canal had water: wrong, corrected.
lessons.how: Sewer pieces: a water brush at z 267 to 291 in the channel, walks at about z 400 to 420 either side. Valve's Route Kanal (reference for shape only; the owner's canal stays dry): water stands 92 deep (60 to 106) in the city canal's dish (168 in d1_canals_01a), 34 (28 to 95) in the wide airboat canals, slime 15 to 32; the depth comes from the floor's dish, the walls stay the same (Route Kanal pictures R1, R3, R17).

lessons.title: Round means round
lessons.rule: A round room or yard drawn with 64 squares has a jagged, sawtooth wall: build the wall from angled segments on the squares' line (the squares behind only seal).
lessons.why: Review, 20 November: the cistern and the chimney yard.
lessons.how: m.shapes prisms. Valve: round pillars are one brush of 8 or 16 sides (radius median 90 in the city maps), canal tunnel rings 32 sides (radius about 512); curved walls step at 22.5 degrees (961 faces in the canals).

lessons.title: A window inside matches a window outside
lessons.rule: Never lay glass on the inside of a solid wall where the front has no window: put the room's window where the facade has one, or leave it out.
lessons.why: Review, 20 November: the flats' kitchens.
lessons.how: The facade knows its windows: a module can ask for its own.

lessons.title: A module's viewpoints stand where a player can
lessons.rule: Each m.view is a place a player can stand, looking at what it names: not inside a prop's box, not facing a wall.
lessons.why: Review, 20 November: views inside props or walls in the checkpoint, tram, lift and playground.
lessons.how: Rebuild the sheet after moving things (map_modules_check.py --only NAME --views DIR).
lessons.check: map_lint.py view (a module's viewpoint inside a prop or a brush, by the brush's own planes)

lessons.title: Look with the viewer, but economically
lessons.rule: Pass the free checks first; then one module sheet (six views in one picture) per module is the cheapest full look; single small pictures (800 by 520) for a detail. The viewer draws props as boxes of their true size and ignores pitch and roll.
lessons.why: The owner, 20 November: the viewer "has eaten about 10x more usage than a usual chat"; later allowed freely for the showrooms on Opus 5.5.
lessons.how: map_modules_check.py --only NAME --views DIR; map_view.py --size 800 520.

lessons.title: A roof needs a house under it and air over it
lessons.rule: Things on a roof need the building to go back far enough to stand on (not a wall one square deep), and the sky must not sit directly on the roof (a skybox brush on the roof buries anything placed there). Keep the sky directly on top only along the map's outer edge, where it seals.
lessons.why: Found building the town's roofline, 20 November: the first chimneys stood in the void behind one-square walls; the leak check caught them (entities outside the sealed space).
lessons.how: map_town.town_plan: plan.fill (640 behind every front), TownPlan.build (sky from the lid over inner roofs, on the roof only at the edge).
lessons.check: the build's flood check (entities outside the sealed space)

lessons.title: Line rooms only where there is wall
lessons.rule: Two-tone plaster, a dado rail and skirting are thin detail brushes on the room side of each wall, and only along the stretches where the plan has wall, never across a doorway.
lessons.why: The owner's flats (picture 05); the town's flats, 20 November.
lessons.how: map_town.lining(m, u1, v1, u2, v2, floor, ceil, low, high): reads the plan's squares to skip doorways.

lessons.title: Build in the owner's palette
lessons.rule: Prefer the materials and models the owner's own map uses (_dev/reference/city18/palette.json: 503 materials, 238 models, by count), so a piece looks like their city when it is stitched in. Their wood: wood/woodwall006a (panelling and trims), woodfloor006b and 007a (floors), woodstair002a/c (stairs), wooddoor042a. Steel: metal/metalhull010c. Grates: metalgrate016a, 013b, metalcombinegrate001a. Floors: concretefloor031a, 013a, 006a, 016a with a 039b kerb. Tiles: tilefloor009a, 007b, tilewall009b/d. Chain link: effects/metalfence007a (the tools use metal/metalfence007a: to change once the modules are done). The Combine: metalcombine001/002, citadel_metalwall090a/072c/077a.
lessons.why: Counted in c18_lc.vmf, 20 November: wood/woodbeam001a, metal/metalhull003a and metal/metalfence007a, the tools' defaults, are not in it at all.
lessons.how: Pick from palette.json; map_town's trims are wood/woodwall006a since 20 November. Valve keeps a place to few materials: a 512 cube of play space holds a median 5 materials (p90 15) from 2 or 3 kinds (city maps and canals alike).
lessons.check: map_lint.py palette (one LOOK line naming the commonest materials City 18 never uses)

lessons.title: No two surfaces flush in one plane
lessons.rule: Two visible faces of different brushes must never lie in the same plane facing the same way where they overlap: they flicker through each other (z-fighting). Sink one piece 1 unit into the other (a sill 1 into the opening, a lintel 1 down into it, a crossbar 1 proud of the bars, a jamb 1 past the band's end, a trim along one wall 1 inside the trim it crosses), or stop one 1 short.
lessons.why: The owner, 21 November: "please also check for overlapping textures on two surfaces that are flush on the same grid/coordinates". The first run found about 300 in one showroom and 900 in the town; most came from shared code (the canal fence's rails at corners, the canal trims where two walls meet, bar rows' crossbars, the town's sills, lintels, door frames and pilasters), fixed there.
lessons.how: Leave a 1 unit step between pieces that meet; map_build.fence, bar_row and map_ring's trims do it now.
lessons.check: map_lint.py flush (axis-aligned faces; a face buried in another brush or looking into the void outside the map, by the build's own flood fill, is not counted)

lessons.title: Copy City 18 itself
lessons.rule: Where a piece needs architecture, take it from the owner's map: their materials (palette.json), their ways (the reference pictures), and their very brushes, lifted as prefabs (map_prefab.py: a box of their map with every face's texture exactly as laid, placed again moved and turned) for facade bays, shopfronts, window frames, door surrounds, balconies, cornices, stairs. Some of their streets get their facades from painted building textures (building_template/*, building_trainstation_*), not brushes: those textures are theirs to use too.
lessons.why: The owner, 21 November: "don't be afraid to more or less rip off and copy the design principles, textures, etc from city 18; the modules are really bad with texture choice and architecture".
lessons.how: python3 map_prefab.py extract c18_lc.vmf NAME X1 Y1 Z1 X2 Y2 Z2 --anchor X Y Z --note ...; in a module: from map_prefab import place; place(m, NAME, u, v, z, turn). The library: _dev/reference/prefabs/ (python3 map_prefab.py list).

lessons.title: Tall walls in bands
lessons.rule: A wall taller than about 256 is never one texture. Lay it in courses: a base (stonewall050c, floor to 96), the body (050a), a band course (050b, about 192 to 320), the body again, a top course (050e). Each course is its own brush, the base and the band 4 to 8 proud of the body, so the wall casts a line of shadow at each change.
lessons.why: Valve's d1_trainstation_01 does it on every big wall (counted 21 November from the owner's upload): one material over 400 units of wall reads as a placeholder, the courses give it scale and age. In every old-city Valve map measured the first change of material is most often 128 over the wall's foot (d1_trainstation_02: 870 wall columns, 04: 1343, 03: 290, d3_c17_13: 781, Ravenholm: 426), then 64; 64 to 83% of wall length over 256 tall is banded, against 15% in the Citadel.
lessons.how: Stack boxes by height with the materials above (Mod.box per course), or lift a banded piece of wall with map_prefab.py. City 18's own stone (stonewall050f) fits the same scheme. Route Kanal's deep canals (d1_canals_08, 12, 13): walls lean back about 14 degrees off upright, step 36 at about 352 up and carry a coping at the top, 476 to 508 over the floor (Route Kanal picture R4).
lessons.check: map_lint.py bare: a face of one material 384 long and 256 tall with nothing within 24 in front of it (printed by every build as LOOK: bare).

lessons.title: Columns on a rhythm
lessons.rule: Big halls and long walls are broken into bays by columns, pilasters or posts at one steady spacing (Valve: 368 along the platforms, 198 in narrower halls), with beams or trusses over them; benches, bins and fences are set out on the same rhythm.
lessons.why: Valve's station (pictures V5, V6, V10, V11): a long blank wall or open hall gives the eye nothing to measure; bays make the space read and give cover and corners.
lessons.how: In a hall module, place a column every 320 to 384 (a multiple of 64 that divides the length), a beam between their tops, and dress each bay the same way with small variations.
lessons.check: map_lint.py bare: a face of one material 384 long and 256 tall with nothing within 24 in front of it (printed by every build as LOOK: bare).

lessons.title: Light in pools, not floods
lessons.rule: Let places be dim and light them in pools: a fixture over each door, each way on and each thing to look at, with darker stretches between. Valve lights the whole train station with 23 light, 40 light_spot and 19 point_spotlight.
lessons.why: Pictures V3 and V8: the lit doorway at the end of a dark passage leads the player there without a word (house rule 10, let the world show it). Evenly lit rooms look flat. Ravenholm: 26 lights in the whole town, its 11 spotlights about 500 apart; the flats: plain lights at 8 as fill and light_spot at 400.
lessons.how: One fixture per bay or door, about a third left off (as the canal walls do), light_spot under lamps that hang; brighter where people gather. Route Kanal: cage lamps on the canal walls about 811 apart (581 to 956), 311 up, each with its own light (brightness about 70); light_spot brightness 1200 (500 to 1850); 346 of 523 lights warm.
lessons.check: map_lint.py offlamp checks that an off lamp has no light; pools are judged in the viewer.

lessons.title: Clutter on the edges
lessons.rule: Dress floors with small loose things (bottles, cans, papers, boxes, suitcases, crates, push carts) along walls, at column feet and in corners, never in the walking line, plus decals and overlays (Valve: 178 physics props, 116 decals and 29 overlays in one station).
lessons.why: Picture V3: the crates and the cabinet hug one wall and leave the way clear; clutter in the walking line only blocks people, clutter on the edges makes a place lived in.
lessons.how: Mod.grime for decals; small physics props through m.dynamic (never prop_static, vbsp deletes them: physics-props-dynamic). Keep a clear lane 96 wide through every room and door. Route Kanal: within 224 of the canal's middle about 4 fixed and 4 loose props per 1024 of city canal, about 1 in the wide canals (the boat's lane clear); commonest oildrum001 264 (and 141 explosive), shrub_01a 190, driftwood 238, ivy_01 110, wood crates 184, rebar 97, cargo containers 93, concrete debris piles 74. Ours scatters about 2.4 per 1024 in a plain stretch. Measured wall gaps (21 November): 45% of statics and 16% of physics props touch a wall, another 4% and 22% within 16; 31% of statics and 25% of physics stand more than 128 from any wall (yard and canal clutter in groups).
lessons.check: map_lint.py overlap and map_floating.py catch clutter inside or above things; the clear lane is judged in the viewer.

lessons.title: Streets in Valve's proportions
lessons.rule: A City 17 street is about 640 to 768 wall to wall: a roadway of 256 (320 on the main war street), pavements of 128 to 192 each side, fronts 576 to 672 tall over it (height about half the width). Side streets and war-torn ones are lower (walls 256 to 384).
lessons.why: Cross-sections through outdoor AI nodes (21 November): d1_trainstation_04, 36 with a kerb each side: road 256 (30 of 36), pavements 192, 128, 256, wall to wall 640, walls median 576 (height over width 0.56); d1_trainstation_03: road 256, walls 672; d3_c17_13, 83 sections: road 320 (64), pavements 128 (45) and 192, wall to wall 640, walls median 256 (0.31); d1_trainstation_02 plaza roads 416 to 608, walls 672 (0.41). Pictures T3.3, T4.4, W3.
lessons.how: Size street modules on these where the owner has not settled a number; where it differs from the owner's own streets (street-profile: pavements 96), the owner's wins: ask before changing.
lessons.check: review (the viewer from a pavement eye)

lessons.title: Upper storeys and far blocks as painted fronts
lessons.rule: Where the player cannot reach, Valve's fronts are flat walls in building_template textures (windows, sills and cornices painted on), with window models (building_tem002_window01 and its _bars) set into them near the player; built detail (plinth, shopfronts, doors, real windows) only at street level.
lessons.why: building_template share of all vertical wall area: 46% in d1_trainstation_02, 39% in 04, 38% in d3_c17_13, 35% in 03 (3% in the lab, 0 in Ravenholm, the coast and the Citadel); d1_trainstation_03 has building_tem002_window01 14, the same with bars 14, courtyard_template002_window 10. Pictures T2.1, T2.7, T4.6.
lessons.how: Backdrop blocks and storeys out of reach: one template face per storey band instead of brush windows; keep map_town.facade where players walk. Check the materials exist in the owner's content first (map_assets.py). Past the template fronts, the 3D skybox (scale 16 in every map) holds only 1 to 47 models, nearly all skybox buildings (row_res_2, row_upscale, project_building01_skybox, buildingskybox_002a, the Citadel, tree cards) and a few ground brushes; brushes more than 1024 from play are 13% of a city map, plain six-faced boxes with 29% of their faces nodraw.
lessons.check: map_assets.py (the materials exist); the look in the viewer

lessons.title: Flats at Valve's size
lessons.rule: A City 17 flat: ceiling 120 over the floor (112 to 128), corridors 64 to 128 wide, rooms about 160 to 232 by 224 to 376, doorways 48 wide and 108 high (door01_left; 96 for a pair), stairs 8 by 12 in their own shaft; furniture only against the walls (radiators under windows, shelves, a couch, a TV), a bulb or dome light per room and every few doors in a corridor.
lessons.why: d1_trainstation_03: floor to ceiling 120 at 81 of 125 indoor AI nodes (112: 17, 128: 11); rooms median 160 by 324; doorways 48x108 and 60x108; radiator01a 16 (the commonest model), shelves 23, couches 7, lightbulb01a 12, light_domelight02_on 8. Ceilings are 120 in Ravenholm too (19 of 41) and d3_c17_13 (87 of 157), 128 in d1_trainstation_04 (32 of 75); halls and labs 248 to 352. Pictures T3.4 to T3.7, R7.
lessons.how: Interior modules: 120 to 128 in flats and houses, taller only for halls, shops and Combine places; doorway 48 by 108 for door01_left. Small rooms work because they are sparse (room-to-move).

lessons.title: Boards nailed across, at Valve's size
lessons.rule: Boarded doors and windows are plank brushes 4 thick, 8 wide and 112 long (or 16 wide and 64 to 112 long), a few across the opening at slightly different angles, in a door or floor wood (wooddoor045b, wooddoor048a, wooddoor015a, woodfloor005a).
lessons.why: Plank brushes counted (21 November): 172 in d1_trainstation_03 (78 of them 4 by 8 by 112), 39 in Ravenholm (4x8x112, 4x16x64), 30 in d3_c17_13 (4x16x112, wooddoor015a), 35 in d1_trainstation_04. Pictures R3, T4.5.
lessons.how: A board helper: 3 to 5 planks of 4 by 8 by 112 across a 48 by 108 doorway or a window, func_detail, each turned a few degrees; for the infestation quarter's houses and the town's boarded doorways.

lessons.title: Wires over the streets
lessons.rule: Streets carry cables: spans of 700 to 900 between poles and wall mounts, slack 100, width 1 to 2; poles 700 to 1400 apart, or utilitypolemount01a on the walls.
lessons.why: Rope spans median 734 (d1_trainstation_02, 25 spans), 736 (04, 46), 914 (Ravenholm, 32 spans from 41 rope entities), slack 100 in all; utilitypole02b 693 and 1411 apart, utilitypole01b 887 in Ravenholm; utilitypolemount01a 8 in d1_trainstation_04. Pictures R3, T2.4, T4.4.
lessons.how: keyframe_rope and move_rope from pole to pole and pole to wall mount, never ending in the air (no-floating-ropes). Rope settings in all 22 maps (781 rope entities): RopeMaterial cable/cable 98% (cable/rope 17), Subdiv 2 (67%) or 5; spans under 128 slack 50 and width 1 (wires between substation boxes, connectors, swings, pulleys), 128 to 1024 slack 100 and width 1 to 2, over 1024 (power towers) slack 120 and width 3; ends pole to pole 276, box to box 24, box to pole 18. Our m.rope defaults to slack 40 and our scratch town had slack 0 to 2.

lessons.title: The Combine is one cold metal; the old city is banded and warm
lessons.rule: Combine places: one metal over whole walls, no courses, lit cold and bright (light_spot and point_spotlight '144 224 240' to '159 237 215'), clean (no decals), teal or blue fog where there is fog. The old city round them: banded walls, warm light ('255 224 144'), grime.
lessons.why: d3_citadel_01: citadel_metalwall077a on 6816 faces, only 15% of tall wall length changes material (the old-city maps: 64 to 83%), 28 light_spot at a median 2000, 17 point_spotlight '147 226 240', fog '67 107 107', 0 decals and 0 overlays; d2_coast_12 bunkers: 27 point_spotlight, light_spot median 2500, '144 224 240'; the flats of d1_trainstation_03: 25 of 37 lights '255 224 144'. Pictures C1, C3, C5, K3.
lessons.how: Combine modules: one Combine metal per wall, cold spots, no grime decals (combine-kit for the props); old-city modules: valve-wall-bands, warm lights, grime.

lessons.title: Ravenholm's dark: weak cold light and warm pools
lessons.rule: Valve darkens Ravenholm without fog: a weak cold sun and almost no ambient under a dusk sky, then pools of warm light from spotlights on the houses (a point_spotlight with a light_spot at the same spot, '255 245 145', 400 to 1000) about 500 apart, dim fills of 8 under them, and the orange glow of a fire.
lessons.why: d1_town_03: light_environment '175 230 239' at 50, ambient '43 45 57' at 5 (the City 17 maps: '237 218 143' at 800, ambient 100); sky_day01_09; no env_fog_controller; 11 point_spotlight each paired with a light_spot, nearest 506 apart; 8 light at 8; an env_fire with '254 174 10' at 300; 22 of its 26 lights warm. Pictures R3, R4.
lessons.how: One map has one sun, so map_raven.py's sheet of toolsblocklight under the quarter's sky is the right stand-in for Valve's weak sun; what Valve adds is the pools: a light_spotlight01_lamp on a house wall every 500 or so with a point_spotlight and a light_spot, a fire in a drum, against the gloom lights (now four at 7, cold grey). Ask the owner before changing the quarter's light.
lessons.check: review (a screenshot from the owner: the quarter's light is a first guess)

lessons.title: Ravenholm's lanes: house to house, timber and plaster
lessons.rule: Ravenholm's lanes have no kerb and no pavement: cobbles and uneven ground run house to house, 384 to 768 wall to wall; houses two or three storeys (walls 256 to 512 over the lane), timber and plaster on a concrete plinth (to 128, 48 or 16), roofs pitched 20 to 35 degrees in corrugated metal or tile, a steep mansard or spire for a landmark; boards on openings, wires overhead.
lessons.why: d1_town_03: no kerb in 119 cross-sections; 36% of the floor is displacement; wall to wall most often 640; walls median 352 (height over width 0.42); woodfloor005a the commonest material (961 faces), plasterwall029a/c/d/g, brickwall048a/d/i, concretewall032d under plaster or metal (first change at 128, 48, 16); roof pitch 25 degrees (31 faces), 20, 35, steep faces 65 to 70; metalwall026a and 014a, tileroof003a and 004b. Pictures R1 to R3.
lessons.how: The quarter's main street keeps the owner's street recipe (they asked for it); use these numbers for the lanes, yards and back ways behind it and for the houses' looks.

lessons.title: A way over the roofs
lessons.rule: Give an overrun quarter a second way through above the dead: low roofs joined by plank bridges and ladders, timber scaffolds, one high place to hold (Grigori's roof), reached from inside a house.
lessons.why: d1_town_03: 74% of the AI nodes are outdoors, many on roofs; metalladder002 4 and 002b 2, plank bridges of woodfloor005a; npc_monk on a roof at z -3096, about 500 over the streets; explosive barrels set on roofs for the roof zombies. Pictures R4, R6.
lessons.how: In map_raven.py: two or three houses with a stair to a flat roof, planks to the next roof, a ladder down at the far end.
lessons.check: review; valid-viewpoints for spots on the roofs

lessons.title: Traps lying ready, the dead from makers
lessons.rule: Leave traps as loose physics props where the dead come: propane tanks in clusters of 2 to 6, explosive barrels in twos and threes, saw blades to throw, one rigged machine trap at a choke point; bring the dead with npc_maker and npc_template_maker and walk them in with aiscripted_schedule; health kits as rewards.
lessons.why: d1_town_03: 13 propane_tank001a, 10 oildrum001_explosive, 4 sawblade001a, a propeller trap (engine, blade, lever, func_rotating); 15 npc_zombie and 2 npc_fastzombie, 10 npc_maker, 7 npc_template_maker, 14 aiscripted_schedule; 18 item_healthkit. The same machinery map_raven.py uses. Pictures R5, R7.
lessons.how: map_raven.py: clusters of tanks and barrels along the makers' walk and one trap at a choke; keep them physics (physics-props-dynamic).

lessons.title: Abandoned shows as litter, ivy and leaves; one corpse tells the rest
lessons.rule: Dress an overrun quarter with trash, ivy and dead-leaf decals and a few scorch marks rather than blood (Valve's Ravenholm has none); a corpse is a single set piece (a pinned ragdoll with crows round it), not scattered.
lessons.why: d1_town_03: 82 infodecal, 0 of them blood: trashdecal01a 26, ivy03 19, leaves_ground02 17, plaster020a 5, graffiti; 2 info_overlay, both scorch1; 1 prop_ragdoll (corpse1) with 5 npc_crow. Picture R6.
lessons.how: Mod.grime with trash, ivy and leaves in the quarter; at most one corpse scene a yard (the zombies bring their own blood in game).

lessons.title: The quarter's sound: four soundscapes and placed scares
lessons.rule: Name d1_town.Street outside, d1_town.WoodBuilding or d1_town.ConcreteBuilding inside by what the house is made of, d1_town.CorpseRoom where the dead wait; put one-shot sounds (a metal grate, a far fast-zombie call, an attack, a fire loop) where something should startle.
lessons.why: d1_town_03: 7 env_soundscape (ConcreteBuilding 3, Street 2, WoodBuilding 1, CorpseRoom 1), radius 128; 27 ambient_generic: zo_attack2 4, metalgrate3 4, fz_alert_far1 3, tram_hit1 2, smallfireloop 2.
lessons.how: m.soundscape with these names in map_raven.py (map_modules SCAPES already has d1_town.WoodBuilding as 'house').

lessons.title: A canal floor falls to its middle
lessons.rule: Let the canal's floor fall gently from the walls to the middle line: Valve's city canal dishes about 88 over its 512 (the floor meets the walls 44 up, median), its wide canals 36 to 48 over 1024 (8 to 10 degrees). Keep the owner's 45 degree banks at the walls (they asked for the sloped sides) and the dry mud; sag the mud between the banks' feet 16 to 32 toward the middle line, so water would run down the middle.
lessons.why: Measured across 372 open cuts of the 13 Route Kanal maps (21 November): the floor meets the walls 44 up (city canal) and 90 up (wide canals) at the median, few floors are flat; true 45 degree banks only in d1_canals_10, and there 284 high. Route Kanal pictures (_dev/reference/valve_canals/) R1, R3, R5, R17.
lessons.how: The canal's mud displacement (Channel.dress / dress_canal_walls): lower its middle rows 16 to 32 under F, keeping the edges at F where they meet the banks and at every module's ends (u 0 and L stay the plain section).
lessons.check: review (a cut across in the viewer: map_view.py --eye on the floor looking along, or a slice)

lessons.title: Long canal stretches get a walk along one wall
lessons.rule: Most of Valve's canal has a ledge a person can walk along on at least one side: in the city canal 72 wide (42 to 106) at 212 up (146 to 256), in the wide canals 102 wide (64 to 148) at 316 up, railed with handrail04 props (40 high) where it is high. Give some modules (not every one) a walk on one wall, 64 to 128 wide, 128 to 256 over the floor, reached by steps or a ladder, ending on the plain section at u 0 and L.
lessons.why: 28 of 36 city canal cuts and 200 of 318 wide canal cuts have a walkable ledge (32 wide or more, 72 clear over it). Route Kanal pictures (_dev/reference/valve_canals/) R2, R7, R8, R18.
lessons.how: m.det for the slab (canal_wall material, a quay_floor top) with m.taken over it so ribs and stubs keep clear; m.no_bank under it; handrail04_long props every 128 along its open edge when it is over 64 up; a ladder (m.ladder, pieces of 128) or m.steps to reach it.

lessons.title: Drain outfalls: big round holes in a ring
lessons.rule: An outfall in a canal wall is a round hole 128 across running deep into the wall (Valve: 588 deep, 420 to 966), framed by the canal_cap001 ring (154 across), its middle about 139 over the floor (93 to 172), in groups about 384 apart (288 to 768), sometimes a pair either side of a wall's middle; a concrete drain stain (decalconcretedrain002a) under each.
lessons.why: 65 canal_cap001 placed across the 13 maps, 58 with their holes measured. Our drain stubs are 48 across at 176 up, one per wall per 1024: too small and too even. Route Kanal pictures (_dev/reference/valve_canals/) R13.
lessons.how: Channel.dress's stubs: a hole 128 across (an octagon prism of black inside, as now, 40 to 64 deep is enough to read) with canal_cap001 on the wall face, centre at F + 140; place them in twos or threes 384 apart rather than one every 1024; keep the drain decal under each.
lessons.check: map_assets.py (canal_cap001 is a static model: check it passes), then review

lessons.title: Canal lamps every 600 to 950, each with its own light
lessons.rule: Valve hangs light_cagelight02_on on the canal walls about 811 apart (581 to 956), 311 over the canal floor (233 to 342), and gives every lit one its own light within 96 (brightness about 70). Ours are 1536 apart at 260 up: halve the spacing in long stretches and lift them, keeping the dead ones and the dark gaps the pools need.
lessons.why: 100 cage lamps measured in the 13 maps; 99 have a light within 96. The whole of Route Kanal has only 208 light, 315 light_spot and 68 point_spotlight: few lights, but on a steady rhythm along the water. Route Kanal pictures (_dev/reference/valve_canals/) R12.
lessons.how: dress_canal_walls: a lamp on every other rib (1024) or on ribs set 768 apart, at F + 300, about one in four dead; the light 30 out from the wall, brightness 60 to 80.
lessons.check: map_lint.py offlamp (an off lamp has no light), then review

lessons.title: The canal's top fence is mostly fence props
lessons.rule: Fence the canal's wall tops with Valve's fence props end to end rather than brush sheets: fence03a (108 high, 260 long) or exterior_fence002e (152 high, 512 long), feet on the wall top; canal_bridge_railing01 or 02 (32 to 40 high) on bridges. Ask the owner before changing the fence they already have (they asked for fencing along the top).
lessons.why: Valve placed 190 fence03a (258 apart: end to end) and 171 exterior_fence002e on canal tops; its brush rails (metalrail013a/b/c, 1,292 faces) are railings on walks and stairs, and brush chain link (metalfence004a, 205 faces) is rare. The house lesson props-not-brushes says the same. Ours is a brush chain link (metalfence007a).
lessons.how: map_build.fence: along each run, a fence03a every 260 (or exterior_fence002e every 512) at the wall's top, yawed along the run; posts come with the model.
lessons.check: map_assets.py, map_floating.py (each fence touches the wall top), then review

lessons.title: Culverts and pipes in Valve's sizes
lessons.rule: Culverts off a canal: box culverts 512 wide by 224 to 256 high (our gate is already this) with their floors dished 64 into the walls; round pipes 344 to 384 across; arches 320 wide and 256 to 352 high; big box tunnels 704 by 288 to 352. A culvert's mouth is a hole 252 to 260 high in a wall 48 to 80 thick; small openings are closed by canal_bars002 (128 wide, 124 high).
lessons.why: 128 tunnel cuts across the 13 maps: round pipes 384 across the commonest (19), then box culverts 512 by 256 (9). Route Kanal pictures (_dev/reference/valve_canals/) R6, R9, R12.
lessons.how: New tunnel or drain modules: use these sizes; round pipes as octagon or 16-sided prisms (true-curves), bars as canal_bars002 props, a little water or slime only where the owner's sewers join (canal-water).

lessons.title: Vary the canal between its ends
lessons.rule: Valve's canal changes its cross-section from stretch to stretch: 512 (city) and 1024 (wide canals) are the commonest widths, but cuts run from 320 to 1216, walls step between 256 and 512 high, and in d1_canals_01 a narrow wet channel (432 wide, 188 deep) runs inside a wider dry one. Modules must start and end on our plain section (512, floor F), but in their middle they may widen into a basin, step a wall back to a ledge, or sink a narrower channel in the floor.
lessons.why: 372 open cuts: width 128 up 1024 in 70, 896 in 23, 832 in 21, 512 in 20, 704 in 19; wall tops 512 in 68 and 256 in 64. Route Kanal pictures (_dev/reference/valve_canals/) R2, R3, R4, R7, R9, R11.
lessons.how: m.open with a wider v range in the middle of a module (side rooms go out in +v), m.low for a stepped wall, m.water or a lower floor for a sunken channel; join back to v -256 to 256 before u L.
lessons.check: map_modules_check.py (the ends still match), then review

lessons.title: A lock is Valve's lock gates in a recess
lessons.rule: A lock across a canal is a pair of Valve's gate props, locks_large and locks_large_b (each leaf about 205 thick, 446 wide, 572 high), set 441 apart so the pair closes about 885, standing in recesses of the walls; the next pair stands 5,185 to 7,300 down the canal.
lessons.why: Eight pairs measured in d1_canals_08 (3), 12 (3) and 13 (2). Route Kanal pictures (_dev/reference/valve_canals/) R15, R18.
lessons.how: m.static or m.dynamic (named, to open) for each leaf; widen the canal to about 896 at the gates with m.open, or use one leaf in our 512 canal; m.taken round the gates.

lessons.title: A valve wheel moves the gate as far as it is turned
lessons.rule: A wheel players turn is a momentary_rot_button: an unseen toolsinvisible brush, spawnflags 1024 (use) + 64 or 128 (the axis, none for z) + 1 (not solid), distance 210 to 800 (negative turns the other way), speed 18 to 180, returnspeed 30 to 240, sounds 24, with the wheel model a prop_dynamic parented to it. Its Position output goes to SetPosition on a func_movelinear (the gate or lift), so the gate follows the wheel; OnFullyClosed, once, plays the lock sound and Locks the wheel. A second wheel without the use flag can follow the first by the same SetPosition. When the game opens the gate itself, the same relay sends the wheel SetPosition and Lock so the wheel shows the gate's state.
lessons.why: 8 momentary_rot_button in 4 canal maps, every one with its model parented. d1_canals_05 gate3_wheel (props_pipes/valvewheel002): Position -> door_lock2_2.SetPosition (func_movelinear, movedistance 148, startsound d1_canals.citizen_gate.Move1, stopsound d1_canals.citizen_gate.FullClose1), OnFullyClosed -> canals_sound_lock01 (d1_canals.citizen_gate.WheelLock1, flags 48) PlaySound x1 and gate3_wheel Lock x1. Its Position also turns rotate_exitgate_wheel and _wheel2 (spawnflags 65: no use flag). d1_canals_10 gate4_wheel (props_borealis/door_wheel001a) lifts canals_brush_boathouselift1 320. d1_canals_11 relay_guncave_gateopen: door Open, wheel Unlock, wheel SetPosition 1 at 0.1. Our lc_stash_valve and lc_aqueduct_valve fire once on a press.
lessons.how: A helper m.wheel(name, u, v, z, axis, drives, distance) that makes the brush, the parented model, the func_movelinear wiring and a once-only lock sound; lc_NAME_open / _shut relays also move the wheel.
lessons.check: review; proposed map_lint wire: a momentary_rot_button needs an axis flag (or turns about z), a distance, and a Position line that reaches a SetPosition.

lessons.title: An areaportal in a doorway shuts with its door, never by a trigger
lessons.rule: A portal where a door hangs names the door in its target key (prop_door_rotating, func_door); for a gate that is a func_door_rotating or func_movelinear, the gate's OnOpen sends the portal Open and its OnFullyClosed sends Close. It starts closed (StartOpen 0) when the door starts shut. Never open or close a portal from a trigger in a map many people share: Valve's triggers open the way ahead and shut it behind one player, which would blind everyone behind him.
lessons.why: 173 func_areaportal in 18 maps: 93 have no name and only cut what is drawn; 11 name their door in target (10 prop_door_rotating such as d1_trainstation_01 barney_door_1, 1 func_door, d1_trainstation_05 lab_door); 71 output lines open or close the rest, 62 of them from triggers (d1_trainstation_03 portal_courtyard_doorway1: two strips 60 apart, Open then Close). d1_canals_08: door_locke1_1 OnFullyClosed -> relay_locks_closegateportal -> portal_locks_1 Close.
lessons.how: map_build.areaportal(box, vis, name=None, door=None) writes the target key, or the door's OnOpen / OnFullyClosed wires; today our portals never close. City 17 wires occluders the same way: d3_c17_10a bldg1_door2 and soldierscare_door OnOpen send their occluder Deactivate and OnFullyClosed Activate; d3_c17_05 barricade_1_gate_open_rl Deactivates backstreet_gate_occluder and the close relay Activates it 2 s later; 42 of 46 func_occluder start active.
lessons.check: review; proposed: a portal whose box meets a door's box with neither target nor door wiring; any trigger that sends a portal Open or Close.

lessons.title: A sound waits silent and plays once unless it loops
lessons.rule: A sound the wiring plays is an ambient_generic with spawnflags 48 (starts silent, not looped) for a one-shot, 16 for a loop that waits for PlaySound and StopSound, 0 only for a loop that runs from the start (49 adds 'play everywhere'). Name the game's sound scripts (Doors.Move*, Buttons.snd*, d1_canals.*) rather than a raw .wav; volume (health) 10, radius about 1250, 2000 for a blast, 10000 for a siren. Of two leaves that move together, only one carries the move sound.
lessons.why: 419 ambient_generic: 407 name a sound script, 12 a .wav; spawnflags 48 on 240, 16 on 68, 49 on 59, 0 on 34; health 10 on 377; radius 1250 on 223. d1_canals_05 canals_sound_lock01 (48), d1_canals_07 sound_redlight1 d1_canals.Floodgate_AlarmBellLoop (16), d2_coast_12 bunker_1_alarm_1 coast.bunker_siren1 (16, radius 10000); d1_canals_08 door_locke1_1 has noise1/noise2, its twin door_locke1_2 none. Our m.sound uses health 7, radius 1100, spawnflags 0 or 16 and never 32 (what GMod then does with a one-shot fired twice is unchecked).
lessons.how: m.sound(..., once=True) gives 48; the default stays a loop.
lessons.check: review; proposed: a sound that outputs PlaySound but lacks flag 16 (it also plays at spawn).

lessons.title: A timer sleeps until someone is there
lessons.rule: A logic_timer that only dresses a place (dust, sparks, steam, a far noise) starts disabled, with a random time (UseRandomTime 1, bounds such as 1 to 8), and is enabled by a trigger_multiple when the first player comes in (OnStartTouchAll Enable) and disabled when the last leaves (OnEndTouchAll Disable). A timer the gamemode needs (a train timetable) may run always.
lessons.why: 48 of 50 logic_timer start disabled and 36 use random times (bounds 1-8, 1-3, 3-5 commonest); they are enabled by triggers and relays and Killed when done: d1_canals_03 deadly_steamjet_1_timer (3 to 5 s), d3_c17_13 transition_flickerlight_timer (Enable and Disable from trigger_multiple), d2_coast_12 bunker suppression timers. Ours (lc_ash_timer, lc_underpass_dust_timer, lc_thumper_timer) run from the start on a server that runs all day.
lessons.how: m.timer(name, u, v, z, lo, hi, wires, area=box) builds the timer off and the presence trigger round the place.
lessons.check: review; proposed: a timer that starts enabled and is not on the gamemode's list.

lessons.title: 'When all of these have happened' is a math_counter
lessons.rule: Each event sends Add 1 to a math_counter whose max is how many; OnHitMax fires the result. An AND of two different things (a scene ended and an item taken) is a counter with max 2. A wave that comes again resets its own counter from OnHitMax (SetValue 0). Every counter needs at least max feeders.
lessons.why: 55 math_counter in 16 maps, max 2 on 17 and 3 on 13; fed by NPC OnDeath (55 lines), prop OnBreak (16), path_track OnPass (11). d1_canals_01 traintrackcops_south_assault_counter: cop OnDeath Add; OnHitMax -> traintrackcops_south_makers_relay Enable and SetValue 0 on itself. d1_trainstation_05 get_suit_math_1 (max 2): lab03_lcs OnCompletion and item_suit OnPlayerTouch. d1_canals_01a sewerbarrels_counter (max 4): barrels OnBreak, then sewerbarrels_gate_intact Kill and sewerbarrels_gate_broken Enable. Valve shipped counters nothing adds to (d1_canals_01a train_boardbreak_counter1 and 2).
lessons.how: m.counter(name, u, v, z, top, done_wires, again=False); our lc_nest_count and lc_armory_count already work this way. d3_c17_10b switches_counter (max 3): each control room's relay (force field Kill, generator off, sparks, shake) Adds 1; OnHitMax fires one success relay that ends the whole stronghold's defences, the shape of our administrator's last stand (collapse.md).
lessons.check: review; proposed: a counter with fewer Add lines than its max.

lessons.title: One relay per event, its steps timed by delays
lessons.rule: Each thing the gamemode or a player sets off is one logic_relay whose outputs are staggered (the sound first, the move 0.1 to 2 seconds later, the end a few seconds after); a second relay only for what also happens alone (stop, reset). Relays come in pairs (open and shut, start and stop) and the gamemode fires only relays, never the moving parts.
lessons.why: 414 logic_relay, 2056 outputs (median 3, about 12 at the 90th percentile, most 42 in d1_trainstation_01 scene4_start); of 344 relays called from outside, 280 call no other relay; the longest delay in a relay is 0.2 s at the median and 2 s at the upper quarter. Pairs: d1_canals_07 logic_start_redlight / logic_stop_redlight; d1_canals_08 relay_locks_opengates / relay_locks_closegates (Unlock at 0, Open at 0.1, klaxon at 0, 1, 2 and 3). Relays drive doors more than anything else does (func_door: Open 11, Close 5; func_door_rotating: Open 9, Toggle 7, Close 6, Unlock 5).
lessons.how: Keep map_raven's and map_forest's lc_X_open / _shut / _opened / _closed relays for every moving thing the game uses; m.relay as it is. A relay whose steps are spread over time is stopped with CancelPending when its event ends early: 19 lines in City 17, 17 of them in d3_c17_07's waves (northfront_battle_reset CancelPending on wave relays 1 to 5) and d3_c17_03's nags; Kill is the commonest input in the 15 maps (532 of 5008 lines): what has done its job is removed.

lessons.title: A switch shows its state on itself
lessons.rule: A switch shows on or off with its own model (CombineButton.mdl SetAnimation togglein / toggleout) and a small sprite whose colour changes (0 255 0 on, 255 0 0 off), not with text and not by switching room lights. It Locks as it moves and Unlocks a second later, so a double press does not undo it.
lessons.why: d2_coast_12 thumper_1_button: func_door spawnflags 289 (use opens, toggle), wait 3, noise2 Buttons.snd9; OnOpen: thumper_1_button_model togglein, thumper_1_button_sprite (sprites/glow01.spr, scale 0.1) Color 0 255 0 at 0.2 and SetScale 0.05 then 0.1, thumper_1 Enable, Lock at 0, Unlock at 1; OnClose the reverse. Valve switches or recolours 67 env_sprite but switches only 23 of its 948 lights; 14 env_hudhint and 1 game_text in 23 maps (house rule 10).
lessons.how: m.switch(name, u, v, z, out, on_wires, off_wires) built as the coast's; our wall_button could carry such a sprite. Recipe, as Valve wires it (the owner asked to keep it, 21 November): R3 Toggle switch with status light (d2_coast_12 thumper_1_button, alarm_button): func_door 20x10x12 `spawnflags` 288 or 289 (use opens + toggle), `wait` 3, `noise2` Buttons.snd9; prop_dynamic props_combine/CombineButton.mdl; env_sprite sprites/glow01.spr (`rendermode` 5, `scale` 0.1, red or green); optional env_lightglow. `OnOpen`: `model.SetAnimation(togglein)`, `sprite.Color(0 255 0) @0.2`, `sprite.SetScale(0.05) @0.2`, `SetScale(0.1) @0.3`, `machine.Enable @0.2`, `!self.Lock @0`, `!self.Unlock @1`. `OnClose`: the same with toggleout, 255 0 0, Disable.

lessons.title: Breaking a place swaps intact for broken in one go
lessons.rule: A wall, door or floor that gets blown or breached is two named sets: the intact props and brushes (Kill or Break) and the broken ones (prop_dynamic and func_brush with StartDisabled 1: TurnOn or Enable). One relay does it with a one-shot sound (48, radius 2000), env_shake (amplitude 12, radius 1000, 1 s, frequency 2.5), env_explosion (magnitude 100, flag 1 for no damage) and fire half a second later.
lessons.why: d3_c17_13 bigdestroy1_relay: bigdestroy1_props_intact (3 prop_dynamic) Kill, bigdestroy1_props_broken (8 prop_dynamic, StartDisabled 1) TurnOn, bigdestroy1_breakables_intact Break, bigdestroy1_explosion Explode, bigdestroy1_shake StartShake, bigdestroy1_wav (Streetwar.d3_C17_13_explode_2) PlaySound, bigdestroy1_fire StartFire at 0.5; bigdestroy3 also wakes a prop_physics beam and fires env_physexplosion at 0.5. d1_canals_01a: sewerbarrels_gate_intact Kill, _broken Enable.
lessons.how: m.swap(name, intact, broken, boom=True) giving lc_NAME_break, the relay the gamemode fires (a Combine breach, a collapse). Recipe, as Valve wires it (the owner asked to keep it, 21 November): R12 Breaking things (lesson valve-swap-broken): env_explosion `iMagnitude` 100, `iRadiusOverride` 0, `fireballsprite` sprites/zerogxplode.spr, `rendermode` 5, flag 1 no damage (19 of 46). env_shake `amplitude` 12, `radius` 1000, `duration` 1, `frequency` 2.5 (commonest; 20 fired from path_track OnPass, 12 from relays). env_physexplosion `spawnflags` 1, `magnitude` 50, `radius` 0 (or 128 to 200 with a named target). env_spark `magnitude` 1 to 2, `traillength` 1 to 3, `spawnflags` 128 or 640; driven StartSpark / SparkOnce / StopSpark. env_fire: burning from the start `spawnflags` 15 or 47 (4 start on, 8 full), `health` 30 to 300, `firesize` 48 to 130. func_breakable boards: `material` 1 wood (243 of 349), `health` 1 to 10, `spawnflags` 256; func_physbox freed by relays (`EnableMotion` 154 lines, `Break` 62, `Wake` 24). d3_c17_12 strider breach: a trigger_once sends each strider SetCannonTarget at a named npc_bullseye (health 20, damagefilter strider_only_filter); its OnDeath disables destroyed_wall_1_brush_1, turns on destroyed_wall_1_hole_1, explodes @0 and @0.5, shoots concrete from an env_shooter, shakes, ForceSpawns a debris template and turns on destroyed_wall_1_link (the hole becomes a path).

lessons.title: A hazard that comes and goes is a timer, a relay and switched parts
lessons.rule: Steam or sparks that hurt on a rhythm: a logic_timer (random 3 to 5 s, off until players are near) triggers a relay that turns on the effect, Enables a trigger_hurt and a trigger_push and plays a one-shot sound, and turns all of them off 1.7 s later. Everything starts off.
lessons.why: d1_canals_03 deadly_steamjet_1_timer -> deadly_steamjet_1_on_rl: env_steam deadly_steamjet_1 TurnOn (speed 180, startsize 25, endsize 40, rate 40, jetlength 80), deadly_steamjet_1_hurt Enable (damage 20, damagetype 8), deadly_steamjet_1_push Enable (speed 40), underground_steamjet (48); all off at 1.7. Three of them in a row make a run to time (a challenge, not a wait: house rule 9).
lessons.how: m.hazard(name, box, kind='steam') in the sewers and works.

lessons.title: Every trigger says who touches it, and counts many players
lessons.rule: Set spawnflags on every trigger: 1 players, 2 NPCs, 8 physics props, 64 everything; add a filter only to pick one kind or name. trigger_multiple waits 1 second. On a shared server: trigger_once fires for the first player only (once a round); OnStartTouchAll and OnEndTouchAll mean 'someone is here' and 'all have gone' (a plain OnEndTouch from one player undoes it for the others); !activator is 'whoever did it'; never !player (in multiplayer it is always player 1).
lessons.why: 664 of 808 trigger_once and trigger_multiple use flag 1, 75 a filter (an NPC class or name, the airboat); trigger_multiple wait 1 on 199 of 305; 92 triggers start disabled until the story opens them. !activator in 93 outputs, !player in 11 and in 52 aiscripted_schedule goals. d1_town_03 street_lever_unlock_trigger: OnStartTouch Unlock, OnEndTouch Lock (the lever works only from the street side); d1_canals_07 trigger_room5_detect_desk_movement OnEndTouchAll.
lessons.how: m.ent('trigger_multiple', ...) with flags always given; use the All outputs for presence.
lessons.check: review; proposed: a trigger with spawnflags 0, any !player, an OnEndTouch that undoes an OnStartTouch.

lessons.title: Group by one name, leave no loose ends
lessons.rule: Things that switch together share one targetname and one output reaches them all (Valve's way), or carry a numbered stem reached by one wildcard (ours, lc_swing_lamp_*); wildcards are otherwise rare. Every output names something that is in the map or that the gamemode makes: the game says nothing when it is not. Parent one level deep, two at most.
lessons.why: 482 targetnames are shared (68 groups of prop_physics, 44 of ambient_generic, 17 of func_areaportal, d1_trainstation_04 portal_endsection x4); 30 of 7711 outputs use a wildcard. 98 outputs in Valve's own maps name nothing: d1_canals_01 boards send Add 46 times to train_boardbreak_counter1 and 2, which live in d1_canals_01a; d1_trainstation_04 citizen_DoorBracer and door_bracerProp. Parent depth: 437 children one level, 41 two, 1 three. Our names check calls a name used twice a PROBLEM: a shared name inside one module would need allowing.
lessons.how: Keep lc_ names; list what the gamemode spawns so the check knows them.
lessons.check: proposed map_lint wire: output targets that do not exist, wildcards that match nothing, parentname that does not exist, filtername that is not a filter.

lessons.title: A door the map closes tries again when blocked
lessons.rule: A door closed by the wiring sends itself Close again from OnBlockedClosing a second later, and Locks from OnFullyClosed rather than with the Close (a player in the way would otherwise leave it open and locked). Heavy doors that must never stop keep the crusher (map_forest.crusher).
lessons.why: d1_trainstation_01 barney_door_2 (prop_door_rotating, spawnflags 34816): OnBlockedClosing -> barney_door_2 Close at 1, OnFullyClosed -> Lock; introom_door_1 the same; barney_door_close_trigger sends Close at 0 and Lock at 0.1. On a busy server players stand in doorways all the time.
lessons.how: m.door and the door helpers add the two wires when the door is closed by the map. Recipe, as Valve wires it (the owner asked to keep it, 21 November): R5 Door the map closes (d1_trainstation_01 barney_door_2, introom_door_1): `door.Close @0`, `door.Lock @0.1`; on the door `OnBlockedClosing > !self.Close @1`, `OnFullyClosed > !self.Lock`. prop_door_rotating `spawnflags` 8192 normal (23 of 51), 2048 starts locked, 32768 ignores players' use; `hardware` 1, `distance` 90, `speed` 100, `returndelay` -1.

lessons.title: An alarm is a turning red light, a siren and makers, on two relays
lessons.rule: A start relay turns on a red beacon (func_rotating carrying two red point_spotlights back to back, in a caged lamp), plays a siren or bell loop (16) a moment later and Spawns from disabled npc_template_makers; a stop relay (fired by the gamemode, or by the start relay after a set time) turns all of it off. A one-shot klaxon (48) can be fired several times a second apart instead of a loop.
lessons.why: d1_canals_07 logic_start_redlight: spot_doors and spot_doors2 LightOn (point_spotlight 255 0 0, length 96, width 25, spawnflags 2, angles 0 0 -180 and 0 180 -180, parented to rot_redlight1), rot_redlight1 Start (func_rotating 16 cube, spawnflags 64, maxspeed 350, fanfriction 20) inside props_c17/light_cagelight01_on, sound_redlight1 PlaySound at 2 and StopSound at 14, logic_stop_redlight at 120. d2_coast_12 bunker_1_alarm_relay: coast.bunker_siren1 and 2 (16, radius 10000) and a red glow sprite. d1_canals_08 klaxon at 0, 1, 2, 3. 194 of 197 npc_template_maker start disabled and are fired by Spawn.
lessons.how: m.alarm(name, u, v, z, makers=()) giving lc_NAME_alarm_on / _off for the gamemode (a raid on a checkpoint). Recipe, as Valve wires it (the owner asked to keep it, 21 November): R7 Alarm (d1_canals_07 logic_start_redlight, d2_coast_12 bunker_1_alarm_relay, d1_canals_08 relay_locks_opengates): Beacon: func_rotating 16 cube nodraw, `spawnflags` 64, `maxspeed` 350, `fanfriction` 20; two point_spotlight parented to it, `angles` 0 0 -180 and 0 180 -180, `rendercolor` 255 0 0, `spotlightlength` 96, `spotlightwidth` 25, `spawnflags` 2, `HDRColorScale` 0.6; inside props_c17/light_cagelight01_on. Start relay: `spot.LightOn`, `rot.Start`, `bell.PlaySound @2`, `bell.StopSound @14`, `stop_relay.Trigger @120`. Stop relay: `LightOff`, `rot.Stop`. Sirens coast.bunker_siren1/2 (16, radius 10000) or a one-shot klaxon d1_canals.Floodgate_Klaxon (48) fired `@0, @1, @2, @3`. Makers: npc_template_maker `StartDisabled` 1, `MaxNPCCount` 1, `MaxLiveChildren` 1 to 5, `SpawnFrequency` 5, `Radius` 256, `CriterionVisibility` 2, `CriterionDistance` 2; fired by `Spawn` from triggers and relays (100 lines) or `Enable`; `OnSpawnNPC > schedule.StartSchedule` (aiscripted_schedule, goal an info_target, never !player).

lessons.title: Small things fade far off; cover never does
lessons.rule: Outdoors, give small clutter a fade, the start about 80 percent of the end: shrubs, rubbish and handrails 2000 to 2500, fences, driftwood and containers 3000 to 5000, poles, barriers and tree cards 10000 to 12000. Never fade what players hide behind (a far player would see through it); rooms behind areaportals need no fade.
lessons.why: 2363 of 6970 prop_static and 711 of 2237 prop_physics carry a fade: shrub_01a 2000 to 2500, garbage256_composite002b 2000 to 2200, exterior_fence002e 3000 to 4000, cargo_container01 3500 to 3800, utilitypole02b and concrete_barrier001a 10000 to 12000. Our m.static never fades.
lessons.how: m.static(..., fade=(2000, 2500)) for clutter in open modules.

lessons.title: Loose things turned, fixed things square
lessons.rule: Turn loose things off the grid and keep fixed things square. Of Valve's physics props only 41% sit on exact 0/90/180/270; 34% are turned 1 to 20 degrees and 21% at any angle. Crates are square only 19% of the time, trash 27%, push carts 14%, couches 15%, chairs 32%, barrels 57%. Fixed things are square: radiators and payphones 100%, benches 89%, fences 88%, prop_dynamic 89%, prop_static 69%.
lessons.why: Measured on 8,951 props in 22 maps: d1_trainstation_01 to 05, d3_c17_13, d1_town_03, d3_citadel_01, d2_coast_12 and 13 Route Kanal maps (21 November): 2,193 prop_physics, 6,154 prop_static. Our scratch town build had 93% of all props on exact 90s and 26 of its 42 physics props square.
lessons.how: In Mod.loose (and any scatter): yaw = the square yaw plus a turn drawn from -20..20 for crates, boxes, barrels, trash, carts, chairs and suitcases, and one in five at a free angle; keep wall furniture, benches, radiators, phones and fences on the grid. Crates in a group are never all square (6% of Valve's crate groups are).
lessons.check: proposed: map_lint warns when more than 60% of a module's prop_physics sit on exact 90s

lessons.title: Some loose things lie down
lessons.rule: Lay a share of loose things on their side or upside down, and let things on rough ground lean a little. Valve: 43% of physics props have pitch or roll, 23% lie on their side (75 to 105), 6% upside down, 7% lean under 15. By kind: trash 53% lying, cinderblocks 53% (16% upside down), suitcases 47%, pallets 39% lying and 13% upside down, barrels 28% (41% of barrel groups have one down), buckets 21%; crates 6%, boxes 6%, tables 5% stay upright. On displacement ground 54% of dressing props are tilted, 14% by a small slope (15 or less), against 26% and 3% on flat floors.
lessons.why: Measured in 22 maps: d1_trainstation_01 to 05, d3_c17_13, d1_town_03, d3_citadel_01, d2_coast_12 and 13 Route Kanal maps (21 November). Our helper Mod.prop writes angles '0 yaw 0' only, so nothing we place can lean or lie.
lessons.how: Let Mod.prop take pitch and roll. For loose clutter: one barrel in three on its side (roll 90, raise z to the drum's radius), half the bottles, cans and cartons on their side, pallets on edge against a wall (pitch 70 to 85) or flat, cinderblocks on any face. On a displacement, tilt the prop by the ground's slope (2 to 15). The mattress keeps its own lesson (mattress-turned).
lessons.check: proposed: map_lint notes a module with 10 or more loose props and none tilted; map_floating.py still catches anything sunk or floating

lessons.title: Loose props asleep, junk as debris, fixtures held still
lessons.rule: Set the physics flags as Valve does: start asleep (1) on barrels, crates and trash that wait for the player (26% of physics props); debris (4) on small junk so it never blocks a player (10%: trash 99, boards 38, cans 36, boxes 12); motion disabled (8) on things that must stay until hit (29%: nailed boards 207, dock planks 61, barrels 55, crates 37, radiators 24 of 25, shelves 21, tables 12, couches 11, signs 16), with 64 (free on a gravity-gun grab) on 76 of them. 256 (output on use) is Hammer's default and on most.
lessons.why: prop_physics spawnflags across 22 maps: d1_trainstation_01 to 05, d3_c17_13, d1_town_03, d3_citadel_01, d2_coast_12 and 13 Route Kanal maps (21 November): bits 0:571, 2:219, 3:637, 6:76, 7:254 (rotor wash, canals), 8:694. Valve placed only 3 prop_dynamic_override, 9 prop_physics_override and no prop_physics_multiplayer in 22 maps; standing physics furniture is prop_physics with flag 8. Our Mod.loose writes spawnflags 0 on everything.
lessons.how: Mod.loose(..., asleep=True) writing spawnflags 1 by default; 5 (asleep + debris) for trash, cans, bottles, papers, shoes; boards nailed over openings 8. Whether standing furniture should become prop_physics with flag 8 instead of prop_dynamic_override (physics-props-dynamic) is the owner's call: ask first.
lessons.check: proposed: map_lint lists prop_physics with spawnflags 0 (none asleep) and small junk without the debris flag

lessons.title: Small things fade out
lessons.rule: Give small props a fade distance: about a third of Valve's props have one (statics 35 to 41% of medium and large models, physics 26 to 42%), rarely dynamics (8%).
