Typical min/max: small loose junk, chairs and corpses 1000/1200 to 1024/1500; boards and cinderblocks 1200/1600; crates 1900/2500; barrels 2000/3000; debris 1800/2000; fences 2750/3200; large statics 2500/3000; huge 4000/5000; props seen across open water 10000/12000. fadescale 1 (97%).
lessons.why: fademindist and fademaxdist on 8,951 props in 22 maps: d1_trainstation_01 to 05, d3_c17_13, d1_town_03, d3_citadel_01, d2_coast_12 and 13 Route Kanal maps (21 November); commonest pairs 10000/12000 (217), 3000/3200 (214), 10000/11000 (184), 2000/2500 (167), 4000/5000 (145), 1000/1200 (143). Our Mod.static, loose and dynamic write fademaxdist 0 on everything.
lessons.how: A size table in Mod.prop: under 24 tall 1000/1500, under 64 1500/2000, crates and barrels 2000/2500 to 3000, fences 2750/3200; leave big architecture props and anything seen from far without a fade.
lessons.check: proposed: map_lint counts loose props under 64 with no fade in an outdoor module

lessons.title: No shadow from flat things, no collision on what nobody touches
lessons.rule: Switch shadows off on flat and wall-mounted props and collisions off on soft or unreachable ones. Valve's disableshadows 1: lamps 52%, wall boxes and machines 49%, ladders 55%, fences 45%, nailed boards 45%, trash 43%, prop_dynamic 67%, all statics 26%. Non-solid statics (solid 0) are 22%: shrubs and ivy (55% of plants), flat garbage piles (86% of static trash), canal caps, pipe brackets, pole connectors, power towers, lampposts out of reach (66%) and signs (64%).
lessons.why: Counted on 22 maps: d1_trainstation_01 to 05, d3_c17_13, d1_town_03, d3_citadel_01, d2_coast_12 and 13 Route Kanal maps (21 November): 1,335 of 6,154 statics solid 0 (shrub_01a 190, ivy_01 110, cattails 62, garbage256_composite002a/b 98); 1,609 statics, 369 physics, 282 dynamics disableshadows 1. Our scratch town: 1 non-solid static in 390.
lessons.how: Mod.static(..., solid=False) for foliage, garbage piles and anything above head height or behind bars; disableshadows 1 for lamps, wall boxes, signs, ladders, fences and boards.
lessons.check: review; proposed: map_lint notes shrubs, ivy and garbage piles placed solid

lessons.title: Use the skins a model has
lessons.rule: Draw skins at random on models that have them, and never tint props. 9% of Valve's props carry a skin other than 0, all on models built with skins: oildrum001 45% (skins 1 and 2), cargo_container01 69% (0, 1, 2 about evenly), wood_crate001a 33%, plasticcrate01a 60%, door01_left 91% (7 the commonest), lights_florescent01a 88% skin 1 (lit), light_spotlight01_base 94% skin 1. In barrel groups of plain drums, 51% mix skins. rendercolor is never changed on a static or physics prop (4 dark dynamics only); no modelscale anywhere.
lessons.why: skin, rendercolor and modelscale keys on 22 maps: d1_trainstation_01 to 05, d3_c17_13, d1_town_03, d3_citadel_01, d2_coast_12 and 13 Route Kanal maps (21 November). Our scratch town: 15 of 693 props with a skin other than 0.
lessons.how: Mod.prop(..., skin=None) drawing from the model's skins (map_assets can read $texturegroup from the QC) for drums, containers, crates, plastic crates and doors; skin 1 on fluorescent tubes and spotlight bases that are lit.
lessons.check: proposed: map_lint notes 4 or more of one multi-skin model all on skin 0

lessons.title: Clutter in small groups of one kind, with an odd one
lessons.rule: Place clutter as groups of 2 or 3 of one kind, sometimes with one partner thing, not as single scattered props. Within 96: barrels have another barrel 65% of the time, crates 66%, boxes 67%, cans 76%, boards 87%, shelves 75%. Barrel groups: 156 alone, 72 pairs, 19 threes, 18 of four or five, nearest neighbour 31 to 58 (median 39, about touching). Crate groups: 98 alone, 36 pairs, 24 threes, 8 fours. Commonest mixed groups: barrel+crate (24 clusters in 10 maps), crate+trash (16 in 9), crate+pallet (14 in 11), chair+table (14 in 10), bench+trash (14), bin+trash (13), corpse+crate (11 in 9), barrel+pallet (11 in 8).
lessons.why: Single-link clusters at 96 across 3,307 dressing props in 22 maps: d1_trainstation_01 to 05, d3_c17_13, d1_town_03, d3_citadel_01, d2_coast_12 and 13 Route Kanal maps (21 November); 540 clusters, sizes 2 (median) to 7 (90th percentile). A lamppost is not part of a group: 34 of 38 lampposts (lamppost03a_off) have no dressing prop within 192; benches come in rows instead (2 to 6, 96 to 112 apart, 83% the same way, 62% against a wall) with trash within 70 (45%), a payphone (20%) or a bin (18%).
lessons.how: A Mod.group(kind, n, partner=None) helper: n of 2 or 3, spaced 34 to 44 for drums, touching or stacked for crates, each turned (valve-turn-the-loose), then maybe one partner (barrel: crate or pallet; crate: pallet or trash; dumpster: trash bags; bench: trash; table: one to three chairs).
lessons.check: review (the groups show in the viewer); proposed: map_lint notes a module whose loose props are all more than 96 from each other

lessons.title: Stacks are never neat columns
lessons.rule: Stack things the way people drop them. 17% of Valve's crates stand on another crate, the top one turned (median 7 degrees, a quarter over 30) and shifted (median 8, a quarter over 20) from the one under it; tyres lie flat (76%) in columns of 2 to 6 (44% stacked); physics props stand on another prop 14% of the time, statics 4%. Small things stand on furniture: TVs on shelves (9), papers and binders on desks, pots on the stove (7 to 12 up, 13 to 21 from its middle).
lessons.why: Prop-on-prop contacts (bottom within 4 of another prop's top, 30% footprint overlap) in 22 maps: d1_trainstation_01 to 05, d3_c17_13, d1_town_03, d3_citadel_01, d2_coast_12 and 13 Route Kanal maps (21 November): crate on crate 49, tyre on tyre 36, board on board 28, barrel on barrel 15.
lessons.how: When stacking: z on the lower prop's top (map_assets.size), yaw plus -30..30, shift 2 to 20 inside the lower top; tyre stacks of 2 to 4 lying flat, each turned freely.
lessons.check: map_floating.py (nothing floats); proposed: map_lint notes stacked props with exactly the same place and yaw

lessons.title: A few busy spots, much clear floor
lessons.rule: Concentrate props in one to three busy spots per place and keep the rest clear. In 256 x 256 squares of walkable floor most hold nothing (indoor city 47%, outdoor 74%, canals 65 to 79%) and the busiest tenth hold 46 to 69% of all props; an occupied square holds 2 (median) to 10 (90th percentile) indoors, 5 outdoors. Physics props per 512 x 512: indoors median 1, 90th percentile 12, most 25; outdoors median 0 to 1, 90th percentile 4 to 5. Doorways stay clear: 1 floor item within 48 of the middle of 69 doors.
lessons.why: Floor rasterised at 32 (brush tops and displacements with 64 of headroom, near AI nodes) in 18 of the 22 maps (21 November). Within 192 of a room's key furniture: kitchens 10 props (9 physics), living rooms 12 (7), hideouts 8 (5), offices 8 (5), Combine rooms 2 (0).
lessons.how: Dress a module by spots, not evenly: choose 1 to 3 spots on its edges (a corner, a column foot, beside a door, never in it) and give each 6 to 12 props; leave walking lines 96 wide (valve-clutter). Keep physics at 12 or fewer per 512 square indoors and 5 outdoors (networked-budget).
lessons.check: proposed: map_lint counts props per 256 square and physics per 512 square, and warns over 12/25 indoors or an indoor room with nothing in it

lessons.title: Furniture against the walls, chairs pulled out
lessons.rule: Put furniture against the walls, square, facing into the room; let chairs stand free. Within 16 of a wall: shelves 76% (60% square, back to the wall), radiators 76% (all within 32), couches in flats 100%, payphones 88%, tables and desks 62%, TVs 60%, boxes 60%, trash 51%. Chairs only 22%: 33 to 58 from their table (median 42), turned to face it within 45 in 18 of 20, one to three a table. Loose barrels 32%, crates 38%, cans 12%.
lessons.why: Wall gaps (prop box to the nearest axis-aligned brush at its height) in 22 maps: d1_trainstation_01 to 05, d3_c17_13, d1_town_03, d3_citadel_01, d2_coast_12 and 13 Route Kanal maps (21 November).
lessons.how: Furniture placer: shelves, couches, beds, desks, stoves, sinks, bathtubs and radiators 0 to 4 from a wall with their back to it; chairs 40 out from the table, facing it plus -30..30, one in ten knocked over in a hideout or raided room.
lessons.check: proposed: map_lint notes shelves, couches, radiators, desks and sinks more than 16 from any wall

lessons.title: Tell what happened with a few props
lessons.rule: Let a small kit of props, decals and at most one sound tell the story, no text. Valve's recurring kits: a bunk room (one to three mattresses on the floor, a radio on a crate, a pallet, supplies, a rug overlay and graffiti); the dead with his weapon (a corpse, the gun 20 to 70 away, ammo, blood decals); a radio left playing beside its dead owner (the sound at the radio); a raided flat (fridge on its back with its doors off, drawers and couches tipped, boards and cinderblocks); a kitchen still in use (stove, two pots on it, cupboard, sink with bottles, the drips heard); travellers (a push cart, suitcases, one on its side, a box, by the benches).
lessons.why: Places in Valve's maps (21 November): c01a 2400 6240 -155, c12 476 10948 507, c10 11152 39 -375 (bunk rooms); c03 -801 -328 -905 and c12 687 6445 425 (dead with weapon); c05 7161 1635 -387 and c06 4000 5812 -151 (radio, coast.radio_dead); d1_trainstation_03 -4254 -4712 274 and -4320 -4634 440 (raided flats); -4658 -4691 276 (kitchen); d1_trainstation_01 -3958 -1711 2 (luggage). Fits the owner's 'keep text minimal' rule.
lessons.how: Story kits in map_mods (4 to 8 props, 1 to 3 decals, an optional ambient_generic at the prop): bunk, dead_with_gun, radio_left_on, raided_flat, kitchen, luggage. Corpses as prop_ragdoll spawnflags 4 (55 of Valve's 66).

lessons.title: A loop sits on the thing that makes it
lessons.rule: Put a looping ambient_generic on the prop that makes the sound, a few units off it: sink drips 6 to 10 from each sink, a dead radio's static 24 to 28 from the radio, a diesel generator's hum at its pipes, printers and servers at their machines, fire loops at the burning pile. Triggered one-shots (spawnflags 48, start silent and not looped) are the commonest ambient_generic (129); always-on loops (0) are the few placed at props.
lessons.why: ambient_generic within 96 of a prop in 22 maps: d1_trainstation_01 to 05, d3_c17_13, d1_town_03, d3_citadel_01, d2_coast_12 and 13 Route Kanal maps (21 November): d1_trainstation_03 sinkdrips (3, at sinkkitchen01a and furnituresink001a), d1_canals_05 and 06 coast.radio_dead at citizenradio, d1_canals_11 diesel_generator, d1_trainstation_05 k_lab.printer and tech1 at servers, d3_c17_13 fire at debris piles.
lessons.how: m.sound(message, u, v, z) at the prop for radios, sinks, generators, TVs and fires; radius 500 to 1250, as Valve.

lessons.title: Lightmaps fine near people, coarse far away
lessons.rule: Never one lightmapscale for everything. 16 on what players walk past; 8 on small detailed pieces at eye level (stairs, rails, pipes, trims, a floor under a lamp); 32 to 64 on faces more than about 1000 from anywhere players walk (far walls, roof tops, backdrops, the upper part of a tall canal wall); 64 on terrain displacements, 128 on far terrain.
lessons.why: Faces within 256 of an AI node: 16 on 86% in the city maps (d1_trainstation_01 to 05, d3_c17_13, d1_town_03, d3_citadel_01, d2_coast_12), 8 or 4 on 5% (canals 11%); faces over 3000 away: 64 on 54%, 16 on only 34%. Displacements: 64 on 70 to 78% in d1_canals_01 to 13, 128 on 16% of the far ones; only near ones keep 16. 8 goes on stonefloor006a, stonewall050b/c, plasterwall, metalstair004a, metalpipe009a/b, metalrail013b, metaltrack001a. Our builder writes 16 on every face and 32 on displacements.
lessons.how: map_build: a lightmapscale per box (default 16); 8 from the stair, rail, pipe and trim helpers; 64 for displacements and for pieces a module marks as backdrop or out of reach.
lessons.check: map_lint.py lightmap (proposed): a face over 64k square units at 16 with no viewpoint or spawn within 1024; a displacement at 16 or 32.

lessons.title: Texture scale follows the size of the surface
lessons.rule: 0.25 for what players walk past (brick, plaster, wood, small concrete). Big poured concrete on the canals at 0.5 (concretewall074a, 022a, 004c, 010c); rock and cliff faces at 1 to 2; terrain blends at 0.5 to 1; water at 0.5 to 1; walls far from play may go to 1.
lessons.why: 0.25 is on 84% of faces in the city maps and 63% in the canals, but the canals lay big concrete at 0.5 (by area: concretewall074a 53%, 022a 71%, 004c 64%, 010c 89%, 074c 90%), rockwall006a at 2 on 85%, blenddirtgrass008b at 0.5 or 1, water_canals_water2 at 0.5 or 1. Faces more than 1024 from any AI node carry scale 1 or 2 on 43% of their area (city maps), against 0.25 on 51 to 64% of the area near nodes. A 128-unit tile repeated over a 1000-unit canal wall reads as wallpaper.
lessons.how: Mod.box(tex=...) already takes a scale (map_build): pass 0.5 for canal wall panels over 256 tall, 1 or 2 for rock, cliff and terrain displacements.
lessons.check: map_lint.py scale (proposed): nature/rock*, cliff* or blend* faces at 0.25; a wall face longer than 1024 at 0.25.

lessons.title: Sit the wall texture on the floor
lessons.rule: Shift a wall texture up or down so a whole texture starts at the wall foot (at scale 0.25: v at the floor a multiple of 512 texels, a floor z on a multiple of 128), so the dirty band or dado in the texture lands at the floor and not halfway up. Leave the horizontal seams and corners as they fall.
lessons.why: 35681 walls in the city maps: the foot sits on a 512-texel seam on 36%, against 24% with no shift; the top the same (35% against 24%). Horizontal seams are left alone (30% against 27%) and corners are not wrapped: of 24840 same-material corners only 7.5% continue the texture, no more than chance. 80% of faces carry some shift, most of it from moving brushes with the texture locked.
lessons.how: In the face writer of map_build, set the v shift of wall faces to -(floor z / scale) mod 512 when a box stands on a known floor; leave u at 0.
lessons.check: map_lint.py seam (proposed): wall faces of plasterwall, concretewall or stonewall050 whose foot is not on a 128-texel seam.

lessons.title: Each lamp model has its own light recipe
lessons.rule: Light a fixture as Valve does that model: a light_spot a few units under the model, pitch -90, cone 60 to 80, inner 30 to 45, does the lighting; a small fixture adds a faint point light (brightness 2 to 10) for the glow. Copy the per-model table in the notes (dome light, bulb, prison lamp, cage light, fluorescent, Combine light, spotlight lamp, bell lamp).
lessons.why: Lights matched to the nearest model within 48 (946 lights, 22 maps): light_domelight02_on = light 254 216 146 at 8 plus light_spot 254 216 146 at 200, cone 60, inner 30, pitch -90 (17 pairs); lightbulb01a = light at 8 plus spot at 300, cone 75; prison_lamp001b = light at 2 plus spot at 400 to 550, cone 45 to 60 (12 pairs); light_cagelight02_on = spot 241 214 173 at 1850, cone 80, inner 45, exponent 5, 15 under the model (106 in the canals); lights_florescent01a = spot 159 237 215 at 1200, cone 80, inner 30, exponent 2; combine_light002a = spot 147 226 240 at 2000, cone 35, inner 12; light_spotlight01_lamp = spot 187 234 201 at 1500, cone 35, inner 20, pitch -30, exponent 0.5. Spots point straight down on 37% (city) and 52% (canals). Our m.lamp gives the dome light one point light, and the canal lamps are point lights at 60.
lessons.how: A FIXTURE table in map_modules keyed by model; m.lamp and the canal lamps place the table light_spot under the model and turn the point light down to the table value.
lessons.check: map_lint.py offlamp (extend, proposed): a lit model from the table with no light_spot under it.

lessons.title: Falloff chosen by the light's job
lessons.rule: A lamp lighting its own spot: plain quadratic. A flood or big Combine light that must light a whole yard evenly: a huge constant term (_constant_attn 500000, _quadratic_attn 1) at 2000 to 2500. A fill light with no model, to lift a dark end without a visible source: low (70 to 100) and soft (_constant_attn 500, _linear_attn 500, _quadratic_attn 0), cold 39 64 73 or warm 216 183 105.
lessons.why: City maps: 246 of 391 lights plain quadratic; 69 with a constant of 50000 to 600000, every one a light_spot at 600 to 3000 (Combine lights, spotlight lamps, fluorescents). Canals: 240 point lights with no model near them, the commonest 216 183 105 at 70 (61) and 39 64 73 at 100 (33); 67 lights at 500/500/0. Our modules write quadratic on every light.
lessons.how: m.light(kind=) with three presets: lamp, flood, fill; put fill lights in the dark ends of rooms and tunnels instead of a brighter lamp.
lessons.check: review (the light pools in the viewer)

lessons.title: Cold light on City streets, warm light in homes and canals
lessons.rule: Streets and Combine places: cool spots (147 226 240, 159 237 215). Flats, shops and canal tunnels: warm (254 216 146, 241 214 173). Almost never pure white.
lessons.why: City maps: 36 of 37 outdoor light_spots are cool; indoors 113 cool and 96 warm. Canals: 166 of 262 indoor and 61 of 74 outdoor spots warm. Only 26 of 946 lights are 255 255 255. Suns: d1_trainstation 237 218 143 at 800 with ambient 190 201 220 at 100; d3_c17_13 238 200 128 at 450, ambient 75 96 116 at 250; the canals go from 248 234 205 at 1000 to an orange 235 155 71 by d1_canals_13.
lessons.how: m.lamp picks the colour from the kind of place; the sun stays the owner's.

lessons.title: Trim strips of another material along edges
lessons.rule: Edge walls, doorways and floor changes with thin strips 8x16, 16x32, 8x8 or 4x8 in section, as func_detail, mostly in a material other than the wall (metalwall061f, concretewall037d, stonewall050b/c, woodfloor005a). Ledges and cornices stand 8 (or 16) out from the wall and are 16 to 32 tall, most of them high on the front. Skirting is left to the texture.
lessons.why: 1627 strip brushes in the city maps and 1481 in the canals: 16x32 (239), 8x32 (231), 8x16 (183), 8x8 (150), 4x8 (110); 59% (city) and 83% (canals) are func_detail; 49% (city) and 66% (canals) are in another material than the brush they touch. Ledges along walls: 246 in the city maps, standing 8 out (116) or 16 (65), 16 or 32 tall, their bottom a median 319 over the ground; only 9 at a wall foot. 28 of 32 doors have a strip within reach.
lessons.how: A trim helper in map_build: a strip along an edge, section 8 by 16 by default, func_detail, kept 1 unit off any flush face (no-flush-faces).
lessons.check: map_lint.py bare counts a strip within 24 as dressing.

lessons.title: Cut corners at 8
lessons.rule: Where a corner should not be sharp (pillars, piers, kerb ends, the top edge of a ledge), cut it at 45 degrees 8 units off the corner (16 on canal concrete); bevel the top edge of a ledge 4 or 16.
lessons.why: 45-degree faces between square faces: 1995 in the city maps, face width 11 (8 off the corner) 568 times, 23 (16 off) 265, 6 (4 off) 151; canals 2729, width 23 (16 off) 557 times. 45-degree bevels on ledge tops: 741 in the city maps, slant 6 (4 off) or 23 (16 off); 2316 in the canals, slant 13 to 17 (9 to 12 off).
lessons.how: m.shapes prisms with the corner cut; a chamfer=8 option on map_build boxes (proposed).

lessons.title: Thin walls indoors, thick canal walls, glass set 4 back
lessons.rule: Partitions in flats and houses 8 thick (16 at most); a door jamb 8 deep; canal and outer walls 32 to 64. Glass 1 or 2 thick, set 2 to 5 back from its frame.
lessons.why: Tall wall slabs textured on both sides: 8 thick 400 times and 16 306 times in the city maps (64 only 95); in the canals 64 (337), 32 (326), 16 (293). The jamb beside 29 of 32 city doors is 8 deep (14 of 19 in the canals). Glass brushes 2 (63) or 1 (40) thick; the frame stands a median 4 proud of the glass (67 windows; 86 in the canals, also 4); func_breakable_surf panes 2 x 58 x 99.
lessons.how: Interior partitions in map_town and map_mods at 8; the owner's outer walls stay as they are.

lessons.title: Ground runs into the brush, never stops at its edge
lessons.rule: A displacement that meets a path, kerb or wall goes past the edge: it dips under the brush floor in places and rises over it in others, and climbs about 30 up a wall, so no seam line shows. Power 2 (3 where players walk on it), squares of 512 or 1024 sewn to their neighbours; a blend material is always painted.
lessons.why: Canal floor displacements beside a brush floor (2872 edges): 47% cross it (part above, part below), 28% lie over it, 25% under, 0.6% flush; at a wall the edge climbs a median 34 (472 edges). Power 2 on 66% (canals) and 86% (city), 3 on 33% of the canals, 4 on 1%; 1363 of 2600 canal displacements are 1024 square; 65 to 72% of floor edges are sewn to another displacement; 95% of displacements in a blend material have alpha painted (blenddirtgrass008b 808).
lessons.how: map_build displacements: let the border rows overshoot the neighbouring brush by 4 to 16 (down under a path, up a wall) instead of ending at its edge; power 2 by default.
lessons.check: map_lint.py (proposed): a displacement edge lying on a brush edge at the same height; a blend material with no alpha.

lessons.title: Decals for small marks, overlays for big ones, in clusters
lessons.rule: Small marks (trash, leaves, graffiti, posters, cracks, outlets) as infodecal: four to eight decals for each overlay. An info_overlay only for a mark over 128 or one that must cross a corner or seam (big stains 128 to 600, ivy about 230, sand tracks, drains 96 by 128). Wall marks low, floor litter by the walls, and in clusters: about a third of the spaces get any, two to four each.
lessons.why: City maps: 699 infodecal to 157 info_overlay; canals 613 to 75. On floors the decals are mostly trash (158) and leaves (105); wall decals graffiti, stains, plaster damage, posters, ivy, a median 78 over the floor (p10 28, p90 398). Overlays: decalstain015a/002a 128 to 600, ivy02/03 about 230, sandtrack02a, decalconcretedrain002a; half of them (city) and a third (canals) span two or more faces. Only 36% (city) and 26% (canals) of 512 squares with AI nodes carry any mark, and nine in ten carry 4 or fewer.
lessons.how: Mod.grime as now (decals); a Mod.overlay for big stains and ivy across a corner (proposed).

lessons.title: Corridors 112 wide, rooms twice that, one long view
lessons.rule: Corridors about 112 wide (64 to 176) under 120 ceilings; rooms about 270 across (2.4 times the corridor) and 120 to 140 high, halls more. Outdoors keep one long view (3000 or more) down a street and close the rest within 512: from any spot, half the directions end that close.
lessons.why: Rays from AI nodes under a ceiling, city maps: corridor width median 112 (307 nodes, p10 64, p90 178), ceiling 120; rooms 271 wide, ceiling 139; canals 118 and 340. Outdoors the longest view is a median 3360, the typical one (median of 16 directions) 483, and 52% of directions end within 512 (canals 46%).
lessons.how: Module layouts: corridors 96 to 128, rooms 256 to 320; streets end in a turn, a building or a gate rather than an open run.
lessons.check: review (the viewer from a node's eye)

lessons.title: Broken walls: odd cuts and debris models
lessons.rule: Break a wall by cutting its brushes at odd angles (a box with one or two slanted faces, not a 15 or 45 degree step), then lay broken concrete and rebar models along the break (concrete_section64floor001a/b/c, concrete_section128wall001a, rebar_cluster001a/b, walldestroyed08a).
lessons.why: d3_c17_13: 102 of 1057 old-material brushes (10%) are cut at odd angles, 62 of them six-sided boxes; Ravenholm 18%; with 126 concrete_section64floor, 34 concrete_section128wall001a, 41 rebar_cluster and 14 walldestroyed08a along the breaks.
lessons.how: A ruin option for map_town fronts: slice the top of a wall box with two or three random planes (convex_text), then place the debris models on the cut (map_assets.py first).

lessons.title: Water 32 to 64 deep, with a cheap-water distance
lessons.rule: Where a new piece has water: the water brush 32 to 64 tall, the bed 32 to 64 under the surface, and one water_lod_control per map (cheap water from 1000 to 1500 out to 2000 to 3000). The owner's sewers keep their own water (canal-water): ask before changing them.
lessons.why: Canal maps: 410 water brushes (water_canals_water2 235, toxicslime002a 109), 64 tall (166) or 32 (106); the bed lies a median 62 under the surface (p10 30, p90 71); every canal map has a water_lod_control (1000/2000, 1500/2000, 1500/2500, 1500/3000).
lessons.how: The water helper in map_mods: depth 48 by default; add water_lod_control when the map has none (check the owner's map first).
lessons.check: map_lint.py water (proposed): water deeper than 128; water in a map with no water_lod_control.

lessons.title: Detail the small and the angled; nodraw where nobody looks
lessons.rule: Small, angled and strip brushes go in func_detail; big walls and floors stay world. Nodraw the backs and tops nobody can see (a module shell's outer faces, far boxes); there is no need to chase every buried face.
lessons.why: City maps: 47% of brushes func_detail but only 19% of visible area (canals 73% and 27%); of the detail 46% are angled and 25% strips. Only 22% (canals 28%) of fully covered faces are nodraw, while 18 to 20% of uncovered faces are (backs facing out), and 29 to 34% of the faces of brushes more than 1024 from play.
lessons.how: Mod.det for trims, chamfered and angled pieces; nodraw on the outer faces of a module's shell.

lessons.title: Every idle spot has its own pose
lessons.rule: Where people idle (a bench, a wall, a window, a doorway, a couch, a bed, a stool), mark one spot per person and name its pose: an entry, a loop and an exit. Seats on one bench in pairs about 48 apart, benches 170 to 225 apart, two sit poses alternating along a row.
lessons.why: Valve: 75 act busy hints (info_node_hint hinttype 12) in 6 maps, each naming one pose: ACT_BUSY_QUEUE 27, ACT_BUSY_STAND 10, and one sequence per person: d1_t02_Plaza_Sit01_Idle and Sit02 alternating on the ts02 benches, watching the clock, arms crossed, hands in pockets, looking out of a window or door (d1_t03_LookOutWindow), a seated drinker (drinker_sit_idle), lying on a couch (laycouch1), sitting on a bed (d1_t03_Sit_Bed). ai_goal_actbusy (31) sends each person to theirs with ForceNPCToActBusy 'npc hint [teleport] [$move]'.
lessons.how: Gamemode: the BUSY table in sv_livingcity.lua (sit, sitchair, lean) can take named sequences with entry, loop and exit, played by MakeSequence as now (SeqName skips names a model lacks); new editor point kinds for the new poses. Map modules: lc_busy_<pose>_N info_targets facing the way the person faces (the game would read them; info_node_hint never reaches the .ain). Changing the poses on existing sit, bench and lean points changes what players see: ask the owner.
lessons.check: review; proposed: a bench or couch prop in a module with no busy spot within 48.

lessons.title: Units get more posts than men, in a set of their own
lessons.rule: Give each place units guard 1.5 to 2 stand posts per unit (a plaza with 2 units: 4 posts), so they shift between them, and keep each set for its own units. A post faces what it watches.
lessons.why: ts02: 4 ACT_BUSY_STAND posts (hintgroup_plaza_cops) for 2 plaza cops, 3 at the terminal; ts01: 3 on the catwalk. 29 cops carry a hintgroup and 19 hintlimiting 1, so they keep to their own set.
lessons.how: Editor checkpoint and garrison points (LC.GuardPostSpot): 3 or 4 for every 2 units. Map modules: lc_post_<place>_N info_targets facing out. Changing how the garrison picks posts: ask the owner.

lessons.title: A queue: slots 50 apart, a front pose, a player can hold it
lessons.rule: Ration line slots about 50 apart (46 to 60), snaking where room is short, each slot turned toward the next one forward; the front slot has its own pose, the others a queue idle. A player standing in a slot holds the people behind him. The one served walks well clear (90 to 430) before the next steps up.
lessons.why: ts01 customs and ts02 food queues (ai_goal_actbusy_queue): 14 slots each, median 50 apart, front slot food_queue_front, the rest ACT_BUSY_QUEUE; one small trigger per slot sends PlayerStartedBlocking(N) and PlayerStoppedBlocking(N); the front one waits 30 to 60 s, MoveQueueUp 20 s after one leaves; the dispenser animates as the front one leaves; exits 92 and 427 from the front; a hidden maker at an exit refills (1 alive, every 4 s).
lessons.how: Editor ration line slots (front first): place them 48 to 52 apart, turned along the line. LineThink in sv_livingcity.lua already walks the front one to the dispenser; the player hold and the queue idle would change the line's behaviour: ask the owner.
lessons.check: review; proposed: line slots closer than 40 or further than 64 apart.

lessons.title: A guarded door is a unit on a police post, not a line of text
lessons.rule: Keep people out of a Combine place with a unit standing at its door on a police post: radius about 60 (32 to 128), never leaving it; he warns three times and shoves; a beating only past a line behind him (a box beyond the door); then he resets. His warnings set the world going (a scanner photographs, he raises his hand at the door).
lessons.why: ts01 to ts04: 24 ai_goal_police (policeradius 32 to 128, median about 60, flag 4 'do not leave post' on 15), given by SetPoliceGoal (20 lines); outputs OnFirstWarning, OnSecondWarning, OnLastWarning, OnKnockOut; EnableKnockOut only while the player is in a box 80 x 128 to 304 x 348 behind the cop (OnStartTouch, and DisableKnockOut on OnEndTouch); first warning: a scanner InspectTargetPhoto; second: Plazahalt at the door. The beating never kills (ts04 sets the player's health back to 100).
lessons.how: Map modules: a facing info_target (lc_police_post_<door>) 32 to 64 in front of every door into a Combine-only place. Gamemode: ents.Create('ai_goal_police') and npc:Fire('SetPoliceGoal', name) on the unit posted there; policetarget must be the trespasser's own targetname (!player is player 1 in multiplayer, from memory). This changes trespass as it works today (the chat countdown in sv_livingcity_security.lua): ask the owner.
lessons.check: review; check in game that a named player works as policetarget.

lessons.title: Guards idle at their post until they hear trouble
lessons.rule: A unit on post plays a calm idle (crouched, leaning on the wall, baton at rest) and drops it the moment he hears gunfire, is hurt, or a door near him opens.
lessons.why: c07, c08: cops on act busy hints with Crouch_idle_smg1_A, Crouch_idle_pistol_A, Idle_harrassidle_A (search range 64 to 300, visibleonly 1), Deactivated by OnHearPlayer, OnDamaged, a prop_door_rotating OnOpen (2.5 s later) or a trigger. ts02 cops lean on walls (Plazalean as play and post idle).
lessons.how: Gamemode: units at checkpoint and garrison posts play one of these through MakeSequence (loop in post idle) and CancelSequence on danger, as citizens' busy spots already do. It changes how posts look: ask the owner.

lessons.title: Start a staged moment where a player is looking
lessons.rule: Before a staged moment (a beating, an arrest, a break, an approach), wait until a player is near (128 to 1000) with the spot in a 25 to 60 degree cone and in sight for half a second to two; after a timeout do it anyway. Seen, it needs no text.
lessons.why: 35 ai_script_conditions: playertargetfov 25 to 60 (true cone) with line of sight, proximity 128 to 1000, requiredtime 0.4 to 2.5 s, a 15 s timeout; ts01's luggage shove waits for the player within 500 with the citizen in a 50 degree cone (3 s at most); ts01's interrogation room shuts its door slot when the player is within 150.
lessons.how: Gamemode: a helper beside LC.IsSeen that takes a spot, a distance and a cone, used before the breaks in sv_livingcity_mindsact.lua and the director's approaches; the act and the voice then carry it and the chat line can go (house rule 10). That changes those features: ask the owner. ai_script_conditions itself is single-player minded. City 17 (15 maps) adds: 30 ai_script_conditions, 25 with the actor FOV left at 360 and 6 with a player proximity of 200 to 650; d3_c17_03's supply thrower waits for a 20 degree true cone with line of sight; 5 of the 30 send the same output from OnConditionsTimeout after 3 to 10 s (d3_c17_06a rubble_citizen_aisc_1, 8 s), so the moment happens even if no one looks.

lessons.title: An NPC appears unseen at a doorway, its job already given
lessons.rule: Spawn people out of sight at a doorway or exit and give each its job in the same moment (where to go, what to do, whom to hate); never spawn one in view or leave it standing. The ones that leave walk to an exit doorway first.
lessons.why: 194 of 197 npc_template_maker start disabled and are fired by Spawn (164 inputs) more than Enable (66); 51 'not while seen' (flag 128), the rest hidden by placement; OnSpawnNPC: StartSchedule 46, ApplyRelationship 23, Activate or BeginAssault 19, BeginSequence 11, act busy 10, BeginRappel 6. ts02 spawns at info_npc_spawn_destination beside hint 903 exits (reusedelay 1); passers-by (2 alive) cross to another exit and vanish, the next 10 s later.
lessons.how: Already our way for citizens (spawn and exit doorways, people who stay): keep it for units and anything new. Map modules: an exit doorway point (lc_exit_N) inside a door at each block or street end, out of sight lines. City 17 (15 maps): 364 npc_template_maker in all 15 (d3_c17_06b alone 87), 365 of 367 start disabled, Radius 256 on 347, visibility left 'don't care' on 363 (hidden by placement); fired by trigger_once 264, relays 81, ai_ally_manager 47; OnSpawnNPC 309 lines (StartSchedule 131, SetRelationship 30, BeginSequence 20, FlyToSpecificTrackViaPath 15, BeginRappel 8 at 0.4 to 0.5 s); makers passed are Killed (39 lines).

lessons.title: A squad moves in lanes: each man his own rally spot and target
lessons.rule: When units go into a place (a raid, a landing, retaking ground), give each man his own rally spot where they gather and his own target spot inside, in separate lanes about 130 apart; start the move a moment after they gather; long moves go in bounds of 450 to 1000 with a pause of 0 to 3 s at each.
lessons.why: 45 ai_goal_assault, 112 assault_rallypoint, 147 assault_assaultpoint: rally points by wildcard, 1 to 6 a goal, each with its own assault point; rally to assault median 467 (quartiles 24, 998); assaulttimeout 3 (74) or 0, assaulttolerance 36, clear on arrival (55); c01's track cops: six chains of 6 points 450 to 1000 apart, zigzagging 160 across the track, lanes about 130 apart; Activate at 0 to 0.2 s and BeginAssault at 0.2 to 0.5 s after the spawn.
lessons.how: Map modules: lc_lane_<place>_rally_N and lc_lane_<place>_N info_targets where the Combine or the Resistance would go in. Gamemode: our GoTo per man, or a runtime ai_goal_assault (the unit then needs a state our think loop leaves alone until OnArrival). Changes raids and deployments: ask the owner. City 17 (15 maps): 41 ai_goal_assault, 109 rally and 111 assault points; rally to assault median 94 (quartiles 24, 465), 105 of 109 rally points lead to one assault point and stop (no chains, unlike Route Kanal), AssaultCue 1 on 36; BeginAssault from relays 0.2 to 2 s after Activate; d3_c17_11's dropship troops play 'cower' at their rally points until BeginAssault 10.5 s after landing.

lessons.title: Where fights happen, cover hints behind the cover
lessons.rule: Behind waist-high cover (sandbags, low walls, crates, car bonnets) put a cover-low hint (info_node_hint hinttype 101), behind chest-high cover a cover-medium (100), facing the threat, about 100 apart (56 to 135), in a named group per building, roof or barricade.
lessons.why: d3_c17_13: 82 cover-low hints, nearest other median 96 (quartiles 56, 128), almost half in groups (rooftop_hintgroup 19, bldg1_hintgroup 5); d2_coast_12: 67 cover-medium, 117 apart; nodefov 180 on all. No pinch, guard or enemy-disadvantage hints in any of the 23 maps. ai_changehintgroup moves a squad to another group 15 s after OnFoundPlayer (c07).
lessons.how: Map modules: barricades, checkpoints and rebel camps add the hints with each piece of cover (a helper beside m.static for sandbags and barriers), the group named lc_cover_<place>. The engine's combat AI uses them by itself. City 17 (15 maps): 215 cover-low hints (101) in 11 maps, nearest other median 72 (quartiles 64, 95), d3_c17_06a 55 and d3_c17_07 38; cover-medium (100) only 7.
lessons.check: review; proposed: a barricade or sandbag prop in a module with no cover hint within 64.

lessons.title: Path nodes about 96 apart, 64 to 72 indoors, one by each door
lessons.rule: Lay ground nodes about 96 apart in the open (no more than about 140), 64 to 72 apart in rooms, corridors and sewers, and one on each side of every door NPCs use, within about 64 of it.
lessons.why: 4392 ground nodes in the 23 maps: nearest neighbour median 96 (quartiles 64, 141); tenement 68, lab 73, sewers c05 66, c07 72, c11 68; open coast 141, c12 132; about 2 per occupied 256 x 256 cell; nearest node to a prop_door_rotating median 65. Our canal Channel.nodes (map_ring.py) lays a diagonal lattice about 181 apart (64 cells, odd cells with i + j divisible by 4); the forest nest 160.
lessons.how: map_ring.Channel.nodes: a node every 96 to 128 in the open and every 64 in rooms and ducts; the door helpers add a node each side. Count nodes per map against the engine's cap (4096, from memory: check). City 17 (15 maps): 5271 ground nodes, nearest other median 84 (quartiles 61, 115); the flats and courtyards of d3_c17_05, 06b and 09 at 67 to 73; air nodes 442 in 9 maps, 140 to 215 apart (d3_c17_06a 131 nodes).
lessons.check: proposed map_lint: a module whose ground nodes' nearest-neighbour median is over 140, or a door with no node within 96.

lessons.title: A gate NPCs walk through switches its node link
lessons.rule: Across every gate, shutter or breakable wall NPCs path through, put an info_node_link_controller: a thin box (16 deep, as wide and high as the gap) that starts off when the gate starts shut; the gate's own OnFullyOpen turns it on and OnClose turns it off. Turn a link off to keep units back during a scene.
lessons.why: 9 controllers (d1_town_03 side_alley_gate, c01a, c03 grate, c05, d3_c17_13 5), mostly 16 deep, 96 to 208 wide, 32 to 84 high; 14 info_node_link; switched by func_door_rotating OnFullyOpen TurnOn and OnClose TurnOff (c01 backalley_gate), by scenes and counters; ts03 link_prevent_cop_movement is turned off to keep cops back.
lessons.how: Map modules: the gate helpers add the controller and the two wires. Our navgraph (sv_livingcity_navgraph.lua) learns a closed way only after failures; the engine's own legs follow the switched link. City 17 (15 maps): 55 info_node_link_controller in 11 maps, commonest box 16 by 64 by 72; prop_physics OnMotionEnabled sends TurnOn (10 lines: a barricade knocked loose opens the way), a strider-breached wall's bullseye OnDeath TurnOn (d3_c17_12), and d3_c17_10b's links and controllers with AllowUse npc_combine_s let soldiers path through force fields while they are up.
lessons.check: proposed map_lint: a func_door or func_door_rotating gate across a node line with no link controller.

lessons.title: Where scanners and manhacks fly, air nodes
lessons.rule: Over streets, canals and yards where scanners, manhacks or crows fly, lay info_node_air about 150 apart (97 to 256), about 120 above the ground nodes below them (62 to 239), and through the openings they use.
lessons.why: 1015 air nodes (+79 air hints) in the 23 maps: nearest neighbour median 149 (quartiles 97, 256), height over the ground node below median 120 (quartiles 62, 239); c07 184, c03 165, c13 104, ts02 78; maps with no flyers have none (ts03, c10, c11). Crow fly-to and perch hints 41; strider air hints 61 (d3_c17_13).
lessons.how: Map modules over open sky: an air node grid laid with the ground nodes (map_ring.Channel and the street modules). Our scanners fly by the engine (SetFollowTarget).

lessons.title: Violence out of sight is heard and felt, not told
lessons.rule: What happens behind a wall (a beating, a search, a fight) reaches players as sound and moving things: a one-shot sound fired on short random timers for a few seconds, furniture knocked about, then what is left (a person cowering, a broken chair). No text line.
lessons.why: ts03 relay_beating_start: the citizen_beating sound (one-shot, flags 48, radius 508) on two logic_timers (random 0.4 to 1.5 s) for 6 and 8 s; physics explosions at 2.1, 3, 4.1, 5.6 and 7.1 s throw chairs, a table and an armoire spawned from templates; the victim is left in a cower post idle. House rule 10: prefer the world to text.
lessons.how: Gamemode: raids (sv_livingcity_raids.lua) and unit brutality (sv_livingcity_mindsact.lua) in a closed room: EmitSound on a short random timer and a few physics pushes on the room's props, instead of a chat line. Changes those features: ask the owner. Map modules: interiors keep a few loose physics props a search can knock over (valve-busy-and-quiet).

lessons.title: Under the Combine, citizens look more than they talk
lessons.rule: In the Combine's city, citizens do not greet and seldom chatter; they turn to a player who comes close, to units near them, to a screen or loudspeaker that speaks; a press of E gets one short line.
lessons.why: ts01 to ts04 each have an ai_speechfilter on citizens with neversayhello 1 and idlemodifier 0; trigger_multiples round citizens start LookAtPlayer.vcd (paused on its first event, restarted by OnCompletion), cit_lookatcops.vcd, lookatbreencast.vcd; OnPlayerUse (19) starts a one-line scene or a nag relay.
lessons.how: Gamemode: TryChat (every 25 to 60 s) and the brush-past barks in sv_livingcity.lua could give way to a glance (face the player a moment) and less chat near units. Changes what citizens do: ask the owner. NPC:PlayScene with Valve's LookAtPlayer.vcd may fail in multiplayer (!player).

lessons.title: A raid goes in through the door, and the residents hide
lessons.rule: Units enter a block flat by flat: two at the door, one kicks (adooridle, adoorkick) with the door unlocked and opened at the kick's own animation event, the other knocks and goes in (adoorknock, adoorenter); others hold the stairs. Residents stop what they were doing, run with their arms over their heads (run_protected_all) to a hiding spot in the flat and cower there (cower_Idle, or Fear_Reaction then Fear_Reaction_Idle).
lessons.why: ts03: relay_breakin_startseq begins SS_Kickin (OnScriptEvent01 Unlock and Open, with a fallback 0.95 s after OnBeginSequence) and SS_Kickin_Runin together, turns a node link off and puts a cop on police posts at the stairs; residents' act busy goals are Deactivated by triggers and they are sent ForceNPCToActBusy to cower and fear hints with $run_protected_all.
lessons.how: Map modules: by each flat door a kick spot and a knock spot outside (lc_raid_kick_N, lc_raid_knock_N, facing the door) and one or two hiding spots inside (lc_hide_N: a corner, behind a bed or a counter). Gamemode: sv_livingcity_raids.lua and the citizens' Cower in sv_livingcity_streetlife.lua would use them. Changes how raids play: ask the owner.

lessons.title: Soldiers pin a target in cover before they hit it
lessons.rule: In a fight with the Resistance, soldiers first fire at a spot beside a rebel's cover for 4 to 8 s, pause 0.5 to 3 s and fire again while he stays there; aimed fire comes after.
lessons.why: d2_coast_12 bunkers: bunker_soldier_* hate an npc_bullseye (health 35, parented to a func_tracktrain moving along the player's cover) through an ai_relationship applied by a zone trigger (3072 x 1408) and switched by two random timers (fire 4 to 8 s, pause 0.5 to 3 s); c01: cops hate a bullseye beside the player while he crosses a zone, reverted when he hurts one of them (missing on purpose).
lessons.how: Gamemode: ents.Create('npc_bullseye') beside the target's cover and npc:AddEntityRelationship(bullseye, D_HT, 99) for the burst, then remove it. Changes how fights go (war, rebel ground, Overwatch hunts): ask the owner.

lessons.title: A timed hold runs on one clock, and each wave comes on faster
lessons.rule: When players must hold a place against attacks for a set time (the owner's exception to house rule 9: holding ground against waves, a post, a zone taken), drive the whole fight from one clock: one start event whose delayed outputs bring the landings, the fronts, the music, the radio lines and the end. Each front is a small squad that walks forward through two or three lines and then storms; when the whole squad is dead it resets and the next, quicker wave comes about 6 s later. A few seconds before the end, cancel every pending wave and send one last assault from both sides; after it, keep spawning attackers until the players have left and shut the way behind them. Changing how our counterattacks run: ask the owner first.
lessons.why: d3_c17_07 alyx_atwork_seq (about 285 s): OnBeginSequence sends dropship_maker Spawn @20, balcony_cop1_maker Enable @40, northfront_begin_relay @50, combatsong @55, dropship2 @60, southfront_begin_relay @80, comm tower doors @110, 210, 260, radio scenes @150, 210, 240, 260, 275, elite_soldier_makers @250, 4_seconds_togo_relay @266. Each front: point_template of 3 soldiers via env_entity_maker; wave relays move them battle line 1, 2, 3 then the assault at @0, 15, 40, 70 (wave 1), @0, 10, 30, 50 (wave 2), @0, 5, 20, 40, @0, 5, 15, 25, @0, 5, 7, 9 (wave 5). northfront_soldiers_respawn_counter (max 3, fed by OnDeath) fires northfront_battle_reset (CancelPending on all five wave relays, lines and goals Deactivate, counter SetValue 0) and ForceSpawn @6; a logic_case on the wave counter picks the next wave relay (OnDefault: the last). 4_seconds_togo_relay Kills and CancelPendings the waves, Activates finalassault_north and _south @0.5, BeginAssault @1, and Enables northfront_ and southfront_pressuresoldiers_maker @4 (stock 100, 2 alive, every 1.5 s, schedule 'set enemy and run'), Killed by gate_close_counter OnHitMax @3. 17 of the 19 CancelPending lines in the 15 City 17 maps are in this fight.
lessons.how: Gamemode: a counterattack or held-zone event gets one table of timed steps (landing, fronts, voices, the end) and a wave loop per front: spawn 3, walk them to line 1, 2, 3 then at the defenders, the windows shrinking each wave (70, 50, 40, 25, 9 s to the assault), a wipe counted by deaths starts the next wave 6 s later; timers cancelled at the end. Map modules where holds are expected: three lc_line_<place>_N spots 380 to 480 apart toward the held place.
lessons.check: review; robots.py can count a hold's waves and that pending timers stop at its end.

lessons.title: Attackers advance line by line, by time or when they have arrived
lessons.rule: An attacking squad holds a line (where they stand and fight from cover) and moves to the next only when told: after a set time, or when all of them have reached the line. Lines are about 400 apart. Attackers on a line fight in short bursts and take cover on reload; defenders and posts stay at their cover. When the squad is wiped, one reset puts every counter, line and goal back as it started. Changes how our units attack: ask the owner first.
lessons.why: 22 ai_battle_line (Strict 1 on 15) and 22 ai_goal_standoff in 6 City 17 maps. By arrival: d3_c17_06b battleline1_trigger (trigger_multiple, NPCs only, flag 2, 512 by 288) adds to battleline1_counter (max 3); OnHitMax Deactivates line 1, Activates line 2 and Enables its trigger; lines 384 and 480 apart; sols_respawn_counter (max 3) fires battle_reset (11 lines: lines and goals off, counters 0). By time: d3_c17_07 lines 430 and 380 apart. Standoffs: Aggressiveness 2 (9) or 3 (8), PlayerBattleline 1 on 17, StayAtCover 1 for barricade and garrison cops, custom bursts 3 to 6 shots in 2 to 4 s, cover on reload, odds of cover 25.
lessons.how: Gamemode: units sent to take a place get line spots and move on when 3 of them stand there or a timer runs out (our GoTo per unit). Map modules: lc_line_<place>_N info_targets 380 to 480 apart, facing the objective.

lessons.title: A squad is topped up at each stage, with one medic
lessons.rule: Rebels who follow a leader are refilled when the squad reaches a stage (a barricade door, a gate, a roof, freed prisoners), not continuously: up to 4, one of them a medic, only for the places missing, the newcomers arriving unseen nearby. Our squads are capped at 3 (squads.md) and refilling would change them: ask the owner first.
lessons.why: 16 ai_ally_manager in 9 City 17 maps: maxallies 4 (2 to 5), maxmedics 1 (one 2, one 0). Replenish comes from a trigger_once at each checkpoint (d3_c17_05 barricade_1_door_trigger; d3_c17_11 the roof @0.2), a relay (d3_c17_10a first_turret_relay, d3_c17_10b barney_lead_exit_relay), map start, once a citizen's OnWake. SpawnAlly0 to 3 and SpawnMedicAlly go to makers: Spawn (1 stock, 1 alive) or SpawnNPCInRadius to a 400-stock maker (4 alive, flag 32). 21 medics among 109 placed citizens (1 to 5 a map); 12 top-up rebels carry ResponseContext reinforcement:1. d3_c17_05 support_cit2: spawned crouched at his own busy hint (Coverlow_L, teleport), held with StartScripting until a player is in sight, then StopScripting; OnJoinedPlayerSquad starts a greeting scene.
lessons.how: Gamemode: a rebel squad leader reaching the base or a taken checkpoint could have the squad refilled to its cap with one medic among them, the newcomers walking in from an exit doorway (valve-npc-spawn-job). Map modules: a rebel reinforcement spot behind cover at bases and checkpoints.

lessons.title: Rebels resupply from a roof, and ammo comes in crates
lessons.rule: Resistance supplies reach fighters as things in the world: a rebel on a roof calls down and throws crates (the crate in his hands becomes a real one at the moment of the throw), or a few health kits and crates tumble off a roof edge after his call. No rebel hands out ammo; it is in crates, and a resupply comes between waves. A new resupply event: ask the owner where it fits our economy.
lessons.why: No placed citizen in the 15 City 17 maps has the ammo resupplier flag (524288, as the FGD is remembered); there are 138 item_item_crate and 39 item_dynamic_resupply (16 each in d3_c17_01 and 02). d3_c17_03 npc_tower_thrower: ai_script_conditions (player looks at him in a 20 degree true cone, line of sight) starts LCS_Heydownthere, then ss_thrower (d3_c17_03_throw_from_tower): OnScriptEvent01 pd_crate TurnOn (the crate in his hands), OnScriptEvent02 pd_crate TurnOff, eem_crate ForceSpawn (env_entity_maker) and mc_crates_to_throw Add 1, whose OnHitMax Kills the sequence. d3_c17_12: a trigger_once spawns resupply_citizen_1 (rpg; damagefilter keeps him alive until it is Killed 10 s later), starts cit_dropper01.vcd and ForceSpawns resupply_template_1 (3 item_healthkit, 2 item_item_crate: 357 ammo, 2 batteries) at the roof edge; a strider's death Enables the next resupply trigger.
lessons.how: Gamemode: a Resistance resupply could be a rebel NPC at a roof edge who says one line and drops a crate per throw (prop shown in hand, then spawned and thrown at the animation's moment), or kits rolled off the edge. Map modules: a lc_drop_<place> spot at roof edges over rebel streets.

lessons.title: Combine aircraft cross the sky as scenery, on a loop
lessons.rule: Over a quarter the Combine holds, a dropship or gunship now and then flies a fixed route high up, harmless (neutral to everyone), removed at the far end out of sight, the next one 20 to 30 s later; the loop stops when the place's story moves on. NPC aircraft are new to our city: ask the owner first.
lessons.why: d3_c17_10a firstdropship_maker and firstgunship_maker (stock 2, 1 alive) send the ship FlyToSpecificTrackViaPath @0.2 on spawn; the far path_track (firstdropship_path5, firstgunship_path6) Kills the ship and sends the maker Spawn @20 or @30; firstgunship_relationship (disposition 4 to !player, npc_citizen and npc_barney) is applied @0.5 so it never attacks; a trigger_once Kills the makers. Path speeds 200 to 400, heights about 1100 to 1800. d3_c17_04, 05, 09 and 12b: a 'firstdropship' (no crate, or crate 2: a strider) crosses once.
lessons.how: Gamemode: a flight path is a list of points (editor 'Point: flight path', or a map module's lc_flight_<place>_N); a timer spawns a neutral dropship that flies it and is removed at the end. Map modules: flight paths over Combine quarters, ending behind buildings.

lessons.title: A dropship lands, its troops go straight in, and it leaves another way
lessons.rule: A dropship carrying troops is spawned unseen, flies its route, lands from a waypoint, and the moment it has dropped them their assault starts (gathered at once, the push about 10 s later, a gate opening for them with its path link); the ship leaves by a different route and is removed out of sight. Our Overwatch drops exist (city-administration.md): differences from them need the owner's yes.
lessons.why: 13 npc_combinedropship in 9 City 17 maps (crate 1 soldiers 7, none 4, strider 2), all from makers: d3_c17_11 dropship_maker (spawned 30 s after the gunship's OnDeath) sends FlyToSpecificTrackViaPath dropship_path8; dropship_path8 OnPass LandTakeCrate 4; dropship OnFinishedDropoff: FlyToSpecificTrackViaPath dropship9 @0 (dropship8 OnPass Kill), dropship_soldiers_assault Activate @0 and BeginAssault @10.5, roof_gate SetAnimation open @10, roof_gate_nodelink TurnOn @10.1, sounds @10 and @12. Its 4 rally points play rallysequence 'cower' while waiting. d3_c17_07 dropships land from path_track OnPass LandLeaveCrate.
lessons.how: Gamemode: after an Overwatch drop, give the soldiers their target at once (each his own spot, valve-npc-assault-lanes) and send the ship off along another path. Map modules: a landing zone gets an arrival path, a departure path and the troops' rally spots.

lessons.title: Combine tripwires wake turrets, and re-arm when the room is clear
lessons.rule: Inside a Combine stronghold, red laser tripwires cross the ways in; a trespasser who breaks one sets off an alarm, the lasers drop, turrets rise from the floor and start. Each turret sinks again when it sees no one; when all have sunk the lasers come back on. Destroying the turrets switches the room off for good, and the stronghold's switches turn every room off at once. A new security piece; turrets are the Overwatch's (civil-protection-tools.md): ask the owner how it fits.
lessons.why: d3_c17_10b: 32 env_beam tripwires (rendercolor 170 0 0, BoltWidth 0.2, length 78 to 414, median 202, TouchType 1, filtername filter_combine_s with Negated 1 so soldiers pass) and a trigger_multiple per room fire atrium_turrets1_detected_relay: lasers TurnOff, alarm PlaySound and StopSound @1.5, atrium_turret_1a_lift and 1b_lift (func_door, movedir down, noise Streetwar.d3_c17_10b_doormove3) Open, turrets (npc_turret_ground parented to the lifts) Enable. Turret OnAreaClear > lift Close; lift OnClose > turret Disable; atrium_turrets1_allclear_counter (max 2: lift OnFullyOpen Subtract, OnFullyClosed Add @0.2) turns the lasers on and re-Enables the trigger; atrium_turrets1_deathcounter (max 2, turret OnDeath) turns lasers off, Kills the re-arm counter and trigger. switches_counter (max 3, one per control room) fires switches_success_relay: every laser and turret trigger Killed, turrets SetHealth 0, combinebeam_nodelinks TurnOn, shake, the last squad spawned @1.
lessons.how: Map modules for Combine places: m.tripwire(name, a, b) (env_beam, filter so Combine NPCs pass) and m.turret_lift(name, ...) with the two counters, giving lc_NAME_alarm and lc_NAME_off relays for the gamemode (a rebel raid that cuts the power).
lessons.check: review; proposed map_lint: a tripwire env_beam with no filter (Combine NPCs would set it off), a re-arm counter whose max differs from its lifts.

lessons.title: A fight nearby is heard and seen as tracers before it is reached
lessons.rule: Around a district fight, unseen guns fire bursts of tracers along streets far from the players (pairs aimed across a street 800 to 2000 away), switched on as players near the fighting and off when they pass; walls hit by heavy fire throw out concrete chunks. The fight feels big without more NPCs. New atmosphere: ask the owner before adding it to fights.
lessons.why: 15 env_gunfire in d3_c17_07, 11 and 12b, all StartDisabled 1, Enabled by relays (13): bursts 2 to 7 shots (minburstsize 2, maxburstsize 7 on 12), 2 to 5 s between bursts, rateoffire 10 or 15, spread 5, tracertype AR2TRACER, shootsound Weapon_AR2.NPC_Single (9) or Weapon_SMG1.NPC_Single (6); d3_c17_11 ground_gunfire_1a and 1b to 6a in pairs, 768 to 1989 from their targets at ground level; d3_c17_07 gunfire_rooftop 607 above, 3100 to 3250 away. 50 env_shooter in 6 maps: props_debris concrete chunks, 1 to 4 a shot, velocity 400 to 800, life 4, fired by a bullseye's OnDeath, a sequence's script event or a relay.
lessons.how: Gamemode: during a district fight, a few unseen 'gunfire' emitters between the front and the rear (sound plus tracer effect) on random bursts; map modules: lc_gunfire_<place>_a and _b pairs across main streets.

lessons.title: Before a blast, a danger sound tells NPCs to get clear
lessons.rule: A few seconds before a planned explosion (a charge on rubble, a breach, a strike), put an AI danger sound at the spot so every NPC near it runs clear; the blast then hurts only those who stayed. A change to how our NPCs react: ask the owner first.
lessons.why: 13 ai_sound in 5 City 17 maps: soundtype 8 (danger) on 10, volume 120, duration 0.5, sent InsertSound by relays (5), triggers (3), sequences (2). d3_c17_06a citizen_rubble_demolition_rl: rebels' scenes @0, 25, 50, 70 while they set the charge, citizen_rubble_danger_sound InsertSound @72, barricade_explosion_rl_1 and barrier_clip Kill @75, the rebels regroup @75. d3_c17_09 combine_crusherwall4_ss sounds @0 and @4 round its explosion.
lessons.how: Gamemode: IEDs (ieds.md), breaches and strikes could insert a danger sound (GMod sound.EmitHint with SOUND_DANGER, from memory: check in game) about 3 s before the blast.

lessons.title: In a long fight, only a few dropped guns stay on the ground
lessons.rule: Where NPCs die again and again (waves, a held zone), keep only 2 to 4 dropped guns of each kind; older ones go. Fewer loose weapons, fewer physics objects. It changes what players can pick up: ask the owner first.
lessons.why: 6 game_weapon_manager in d3_c17_07 (the timed hold), 11 and 12 (long street fights): weaponname weapon_ar2 (3) or weapon_smg1 (2), maxpieces 3 (3), 2 (2) or 4, ammomod 1. One is misspelt 'waepon_ar2' in Valve's file and so does nothing.
lessons.how: Gamemode: when an NPC's dropped weapon is made, count those of its class and remove the oldest beyond the limit (or never drop, as the owner prefers).

lessons.title: A reminder stops the moment it is done, and the way opens anyway
lessons.rule: When a player must learn to do something, a person says it (not text) a few times about 10 s apart; the moment the player does it, every pending reminder is cancelled; and after about 50 s the way on opens regardless, so no one is stuck. Text on screen is kept for the one key to press. Valve's 15 City 17 maps put text on screen only 7 times.
lessons.why: d3_c17_03 command_send_nag_relay: command_send_nag_1 to 4 (squad_train01 to 04.vcd, spoken) @10, 20, 30, 40, the key hint (env_hudhint valve_hint_command_send) @0.5, 11, 21, 31, 41, plaza_exit_conditions Enable @50. Any citizen's OnStationOrder fires command_recall_hudhint_relay: command_send_nag_relay CancelPending @0 and Kill @0.1, the send hint Killed, the next hint @7, the exit @10. Text entities in the 15 maps: 2 env_hudhint (squad commands), 4 env_message (GAMEOVER_ALLY), 1 game_text ('You have failed.').
lessons.how: Gamemode: tutorials and job steps that wait for an action: voice lines on a timer, all cancelled (timer.Remove) on success, and a timeout that moves on; one notice at most (house rule 10).
lessons.check: review; house_rules.py already counts text on screen.

lessons.title: Followers wait at marked spots, not on the leader's heels
lessons.rule: Where squads follow a leader, mark spots for them to wait at when the leader stops (by doors, corners, behind cover), in small clusters about 60 apart, and in a base mark spots where people step aside to when someone pushes past. Whether our followers use them needs a check in game: ask the owner before changing how they follow.
lessons.why: In the 15 City 17 maps (hint meanings as the FGD is remembered): 291 info_node_hint of type 900 (follower wait point) in 10 maps, nearest other median 59 (quartiles 43, 115), up to 68 a map (d3_c17_05); 91 of type 950 (ally move-away spot), 84 of them in the d3_c17_05 rebel base, 152 apart; 110 of type 902 (squad transition, about 262 from the map change); only 8 act busy hints, so rebels in the street war do not idle.
lessons.how: Map modules: lc_wait spots (info_node_hint hinttype 900) in twos and threes by doors and corners of streets rebels use; 950 spots round the rebel base's rooms.

lessons.title: A loud approach wakes a Combine post
lessons.rule: A small Combine post (a guard room, an outpost) stays quiet until it hears gunfire or an explosion within about 300 of it, or sees an intruder; then its men come out and hold the room from cover, and when half are down the rest fall back to a second line. Changes how our garrisons react: ask the owner first.
lessons.why: d3_c17_05 outpost_microphone (env_microphone, MaxRange 300, spawnflags 40 = bullet impacts and explosions, StartDisabled 1, Enabled by a trigger_once as the player nears): OnHeardSound Spawns outpost_room_1_cop_1_maker and _2_maker and starts their schedule. outpost_room_1_standoff and _2 (StayAtCover 1) Activate from a cop's OnFoundPlayer. garrison_3nd_floor: cops 3 and 4 OnDeath fire garrison_3nd_floor_cop_fallback_relay: a fallback battle line, a fallback standoff and a schedule to the fallback hint group (garrison_3nd_floor_cop_fallbacks). ai_changehintgroup (6) moves squads to their next hint group from OnAssaultClear (4).
lessons.how: Gamemode: Combine posts and garrisons could listen (EntityFireBullets, explosions) within about 300 and wake their units; a fallback spot set per room. Map modules: lc_post_<room>_fallback_N spots.

lessons.title: A sniper shows himself before he kills, and only while players are in his street
lessons.rule: A Combine sniper sits in a high window (about 280 to 410 above the street), is switched on when players enter his street and removed when they leave it; his laser paints a target about a second before each shot, and crows on the street are shot first, telling players he is there. NPC snipers are new: ask the owner first.
lessons.why: d3_c17_09: 5 npc_sniper, 281 to 409 above the nearest ground node; EnableSniper from trigger_onces (one from logic_auto @5), Kill from trigger_onces past the street; PaintInterval 1, PaintIntervalVariance 0.75, misses 0, shielddistance 64, shieldradius 48; 5 npc_crow below (ai_relationship snipers hate crows); a func_brush (sniper4_los) blocks one sniper's view until he dies; sniper4 OnDeath sends sniper2 SweepGroupRandomly sniper_sweeptarget; sniper_death_counter (max 2) ends the street.
lessons.how: Gamemode: an Overwatch sniper for district fights (a window spot from the editor or a module's lc_sniper_<street>), on while players are in his street's box, with a visible laser lead before each shot.
